units.title: Measurement & Scientific Skills
units.intro: Learners master the SI toolkit using market tins, jerricans and their own bodies before any theory begins.

lessons.title: What Is Physics? Motion, Forces and Energy Around Us
lessons.focus: Define physics as study of matter, motion, forces, energy; tour school compound identifying physics at work (gate hinge, water tank, boda).
lessons.advanced: List three physics careers in Kenya (jua kali fabrication, civil engineering, radiography) and the physics each uses daily.

lessons.title: Science Safety and Workshop Rules
lessons.focus: Safe handling of sharps (panga, nails), heat (jiko), water, glass; agreeing class safety charter; why rules exist before experiments.
lessons.advanced: Write a risk assessment (hazard, risk, control) for three planned course builds.

lessons.title: The Scientific Investigation: Ask, Predict, Test, Record
lessons.focus: Steps of investigation using a swinging stone on a string; hypothesis writing; honest recording even when wrong.
lessons.advanced: Distinguish hypothesis from prediction; write both for the swing experiment.

lessons.title: Fair Tests and Variables
lessons.focus: Independent, dependent, controlled variables via dropping different balls (stone, rubber, crumpled paper ball) from same height.
lessons.advanced: Identify the confounding variable when two balls differ in BOTH mass and size.

lessons.title: SI Units and Why Standards Matter
lessons.focus: Metre, kilogram, second, litre; history of body-based measures (cubit, stride) and disputes at market without standards.
lessons.advanced: A trader sells a 'debe' of maize whose tin is dented inward. Quantify the buyer's loss if dent removes 8% of volume.

lessons.title: Measuring Length I: Rulers and Tape Measures
lessons.focus: mm/cm/m; correct ruler use (zero end, eye level); measure desk, book, classroom, footstride.
lessons.advanced: Classroom is 7.4 m long; convert to mm and explain when mm precision is pointless.

lessons.title: Measuring Length II: Vernier Callipers and Micrometers
lessons.focus: Jua kali precision tools; measuring wire diameter, nail thickness; reading a vernier scale.
lessons.advanced: Read a vernier to 0.1 mm; explain why the extra scale beats estimation.

lessons.title: Estimation Skills: Guess, Then Measure
lessons.focus: Estimating lengths/masses before measuring; calibration of the human estimator; flagpole height by shadows preview.
lessons.advanced: Flagpole shadow 6.0 m when your 1.5 m shadow is yours at height 1.6 m — compute pole height by similar triangles.

lessons.title: Measuring Mass: Build a Beam Balance
lessons.focus: Mass vs amount-of-matter; build ruler-on-pivot balance with debe/bottle-cap pans; compare masses of stones.
lessons.advanced: Why must the pans hang at equal distances from the pivot? Link to moments.

lessons.title: Weight vs Mass: A First Look
lessons.focus: Mass in kg is amount of matter; weight in N is gravity's pull; rubber-band spring balance shows weight changing, mass constant.
lessons.advanced: Your mass is 45 kg. State your weight on Earth (g=10 N/kg) and on the Moon (g=1.6 N/kg).

lessons.title: Measuring Time: Heartbeats, Stopwatches and Sundials
lessons.focus: Second as base unit; calibrating heartbeats against a clock; build stick-and-shadow sundial; limits of body clocks.
lessons.advanced: Why does a Kenyan sundial disagree with clock time across the year? Introduce the equation of time qualitatively.

lessons.title: Measuring Volume I: Regular Solids and Containers
lessons.focus: Volume = l×w×h; reading jerrican and sufuria markings; litre vs cm³ vs m³ conversions.
lessons.advanced: A '20-litre' jerrican measures 24×18×47 cm internally. Compute its true volume in litres and percentage error of the label.

lessons.title: Measuring Volume II: Displacement for Irregular Objects
lessons.focus: Stone volume by water displacement; overflow can made from a tin with a spout hole; Archimedes teaser.
lessons.advanced: A stone displaces 85 cm³ of water and weighs 2.1 N in air. Compute its density (take g=10 N/kg).

lessons.title: Density I: Heavy for Its Size
lessons.focus: Density concept; equal-size blocks of wood vs stone vs steel; density = mass/volume; units kg/m³ and g/cm³.
lessons.advanced: Convert 2.7 g/cm³ (aluminium) to kg/m³; why do engineers prefer kg/m³?

lessons.title: Density II: Measuring Densities of Local Materials
lessons.focus: Measure density of a nail, stone, maize cob, charcoal; compare with water (1000 kg/m³); predict float or sink.
lessons.advanced: Charcoal 'floats' yet is wood-derived: explain using trapped air pores and average density.

lessons.title: Measuring Very Small Things
lessons.focus: Measure-100-divide trick: thickness of one book page, one grain of maize mass, one drop of water volume.
lessons.advanced: Page thickness comes out 0.09±0.02 mm. Explain how the many-at-once method reduces percentage error.

lessons.title: Errors, Accuracy and Parallax
lessons.focus: Parallax error reading a ruler; zero error on balances; repeat-and-average; random vs systematic error.
lessons.advanced: Three students measure a desk: 119.8, 120.1, 119.9 cm. Give mean and spread; decide if a 4th reading of 122.0 is an outlier.

lessons.title: Honest Numbers: Significant Figures and Rounding
lessons.focus: Report measurements to the precision of the instrument; rounding rules; false precision ('the cow weighs 423.771 kg!').
lessons.advanced: Multiply 12.5 cm × 3.2 cm: state the area with correct significant figures and justify.

lessons.title: Designing Data Tables
lessons.focus: Quantity/unit headers; raw data vs processed columns; table for stretch-vs-load experiment preview.
lessons.advanced: Redesign a bad table (units mixed in cells, no headers) into standard form.

lessons.title: Graphs I: Plotting Your Walk
lessons.focus: Axes, scale choice, plotting distance-vs-time of a timed 20 m walk; dots not blobs; line of best fit intro.
lessons.advanced: Choose scales so the plot fills the page: 20 m in 25 s — propose axis ranges and divisions.

lessons.title: Graphs II: Slope Tells Speed
lessons.focus: Gradient = rate; steeper = faster; straight line through origin means proportional; interpolate a missing point.
lessons.advanced: From a given distance-time graph, compute gradient with units and state what it means physically.

lessons.title: Area and Volume Formulas in the Real World
lessons.focus: Classroom floor area, water tank volume (cylinder V=πr²h), roof catchment area teaser; litres↔m³ (1000 L = 1 m³).
lessons.advanced: A cylindrical tank r=1.2 m, h=1.8 m: compute volume in litres and days of supply for a family using 200 L/day.

lessons.title: Unit Conversions Mastery
lessons.focus: mm↔cm↔m↔km, g↔kg, mL↔L, s↔min; km/h↔m/s preview; conversion chain method (multiply by 1).
lessons.advanced: Convert 72 km/h to m/s by the chain method; why does ×1000/3600 work?

lessons.title: Measurement in the Market: Standards and Trade
lessons.focus: The debe system, weighing at posho mill and butchery, KEBS role, honest trade; measure a 'kilo' of unga vs label.
lessons.advanced: Design an inspection: how would you check 10 market scales with one 5 kg known mass?

lessons.title: Build a Water Clock (Clepsydra)
lessons.focus: Bottle with small hole drips into marked jar; calibrate minutes against a clock; discover rate falls as level drops (pressure teaser).
lessons.advanced: Explain via P=ρgh why drips slow as the reservoir empties; propose a constant-head fix (overflow feeder).

lessons.title: Unit Review: Measurement Olympics
lessons.focus: Rotating stations: length, mass, volume, time, density, estimation; teams scored on accuracy and honest reporting; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Combined error: tank volume from r and h each ±3% — estimate worst-case volume error percentage.

units.title: Forces in Everyday Life
units.intro: Pushes, pulls, friction and Newton's laws discovered with ropes, rubber strips, shoes and handcarts.

lessons.title: Force: Pushes and Pulls Everywhere
lessons.focus: Force defined by what it does; hunt for ten forces in the compound (opening sufuria lid, pulling mkokoteni, wind on mabati).
lessons.advanced: Classify each found force as contact or non-contact; justify the classification of gravity.

lessons.title: What Forces Do: Move, Stop, Turn, Shape
lessons.focus: Four effects catalogued by kicking a ball, squeezing clay, bending a stick, stretching rubber.
lessons.advanced: A force changes shape but the object does not move: where does the work go? Preview elastic energy.

lessons.title: Measuring Force: The Newton and the Rubber-Strip Meter
lessons.focus: Build and calibrate a force meter from rubber strips using water (1 L ≈ 1 kg ≈ 10 N); the spring balance idea.
lessons.advanced: Your rubber strip stretches non-linearly. Describe a two-point calibration error and a fix using more calibration points.

lessons.title: Gravity: Earth's Pull on Everything
lessons.focus: Gravity as downward pull; falling mango vs thrown stone; weight as gravitational force; g ≈ 10 N/kg introduced.
lessons.advanced: Why doesn't the Moon fall onto Earth despite gravity? Seed the idea of orbital motion.

lessons.title: Weight = Mass × g: Getting It Right
lessons.focus: W = mg; measure masses with beam balance, weights with spring balance; tabulate and verify factor of 10.
lessons.advanced: A scale calibrated in Nairobi reads your 'weight' 60 kg. Is that reading mass or force, and what error appears at high altitude?

lessons.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
lessons.focus: Tug-of-war with sisal rope; equal forces → no motion change; net force concept; stationary objects have balanced forces.
lessons.advanced: A 400 N pull left meets 350 N right: find net force and direction; describe the motion change.

lessons.title: Drawing Force Diagrams
lessons.focus: Arrows show size and direction; draw forces on a book on a desk, a hanging jerrican, a leaning ladder.
lessons.advanced: Draw the hanging jerrican diagram with the rope at 20°: which component carries the weight? Qualitative vectors.

lessons.title: Friction I: The Force That Opposes Sliding
lessons.focus: Rub hands, drag shoe on floor then grass; friction acts opposite motion; surface roughness matters.
lessons.advanced: Friction is caused by microscopic welds between surfaces: explain why polishing reduces it only up to a point.

lessons.title: Friction II: When We Need It
lessons.focus: Walking, tyre treads on murram, jembe handle grip, writing chalk, boda braking: life without friction skit.
lessons.advanced: Explain why wet murram roads reduce friction and how tread channels water away.

lessons.title: Friction III: Reducing It with Oil, Rollers and Bearings
lessons.focus: Grease on hinges, rollers under debe, ball bearings from boda hubs; sliding vs rolling compared by pull test.
lessons.advanced: Pull-force drops from 18 N to 3 N with rollers: compute friction reduction percentage and where the energy was going.

lessons.title: Friction Lab: Pull Tests on Surfaces
lessons.focus: Spring balance drags a loaded block over wood, sandpaper, grass, oiled wood; force vs load graph.
lessons.advanced: Plot friction vs load; find the gradient — introduce coefficient of friction μ for your surfaces.

lessons.title: Air Resistance: The Invisible Brake
lessons.focus: Flat vs crumpled paper drop; plastic-bag parachute; streamlining preview; drag grows with speed.
lessons.advanced: Why does a falling raindrop not accelerate forever? Introduce terminal velocity conceptually.

lessons.title: Water Resistance and Streamlining
lessons.focus: Sweep hand flat vs edge-on through water; fish and canoe shapes; mould clay hulls and drag-test them.
lessons.advanced: Explain in particle terms why water drag exceeds air drag at the same speed.

lessons.title: Tension: Forces in Ropes and Strings
lessons.focus: Sisal rope tension; tug-of-war revisited with force meter in the middle; knots and why they slip; clothesline sag.
lessons.advanced: A 50 N pull on each end of a rope — is the tension 50 N or 100 N? Resolve the classic misconception.

lessons.title: Compression and Support Forces
lessons.focus: Standing on soil vs mattress; pillars and poles; chalk under compression snaps differently; stool legs.
lessons.advanced: Why does chalk fail in tension before compression? Link to crack opening at the bent side.

lessons.title: The Normal Force: Surfaces Push Back
lessons.focus: Table pushes up on books; bathroom scale reads the push; leaning on a wall; normal means perpendicular.
lessons.advanced: On a 30° ramp, which is bigger: weight or normal force? Resolve vectors qualitatively.

lessons.title: Elastic Forces: Things That Spring Back
lessons.focus: Rubber, springs, bows: restoring force grows with stretch; preview Hooke's law; slingshot (manati) energy teaser.
lessons.advanced: Sketch force vs stretch for rubber: why does it curve up at large extension? (Polymer chains uncoiling.)

lessons.title: Forces Come in Pairs: A First Look at Reaction
lessons.focus: Push the wall, the wall pushes you; step off a floating log and it moves back; pair forces act on different bodies.
lessons.advanced: If pair forces are equal and opposite, why does anything accelerate? (They act on different objects.)

lessons.title: Newton's First Law: Inertia
lessons.focus: Coin on card flick; passengers lurch when matatu brakes; inertia depends on mass; seatbelt teaser.
lessons.advanced: Use inertia to explain why a fully loaded lorry needs a longer braking distance than an empty one at the same speed.

lessons.title: Newton's Second Law: F = ma
lessons.focus: Push empty then full debe with same effort; acceleration depends on force and mass; quantify with toy car and falling mass.
lessons.advanced: A 2 kg trolley accelerates at 1.5 m/s² under a hanging mass: compute the net force and discuss friction's role.

lessons.title: Newton's Third Law: Action and Reaction
lessons.focus: Balloon rocket on a string line; walking as pushing Earth back; rowing a canoe; identify pairs in five scenarios.
lessons.advanced: A 500 N boda accelerates forward: identify the action-reaction pair at the tyre-road contact.

lessons.title: Net Force and Acceleration Lab
lessons.focus: Falling-mass trolley on a smooth board; vary hanging mass; acceleration vs force graph through origin.
lessons.advanced: From a vs F graph gradient, extract the system mass; explain the intercept if friction was not fully compensated.

lessons.title: Combining Forces at Angles
lessons.focus: Two students pull one jerrican with ropes at an angle; resultant feels less than the sum; parallelogram idea by drawing.
lessons.advanced: Two 40 N pulls at 60° to each other: find the resultant by scale drawing; compare with 80 N straight pull.

lessons.title: Everyday Force Mysteries Clinic
lessons.focus: Why door handles sit far from hinges; opening paint tins with a panga edge; loosening tight bottle caps with cloth.
lessons.advanced: Explain the paint-tin lever with moments: tin-lid rim is fulcrum; compute MA for a 15 cm panga vs 2 cm lid lip.

lessons.title: Build: Balloon Rocket Line
lessons.focus: Straw + taut string + balloon; test balloon size, payload (paperclips), launch angle; measure travel distance.
lessons.advanced: Predict how payload mass affects final distance using F=ma and impulse reasoning; test it.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Force Detective Day
lessons.focus: Stations around school: identify, measure and draw forces (gate, flagpole, water tank, seesaw); unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Design one station yourself with a measurable force question and a marking scheme.

units.title: Describing Motion
units.intro: Distance, speed, velocity and acceleration measured on the school field and graphed by hand.

lessons.title: What Is Motion? Position and Reference Points
lessons.focus: Motion is change of position relative to a reference; 'moving compared to what?' game; frame of reference.
lessons.advanced: Passenger in a moving matatu: at rest or in motion? Explain using reference frames.

lessons.title: Distance vs Displacement
lessons.focus: Walk an L-shaped path; distance paced vs straight-line displacement; scalar vs vector introduced.
lessons.advanced: You walk 30 m east then 40 m north: compute distance and displacement; explain why displacement can be zero after a long walk.

lessons.title: Speed: How Fast Is Fast?
lessons.focus: v = d/t; time a 40 m walk and run; compute speeds; compare class results on a chart.
lessons.advanced: A runner covers 100 m in 14.0 s: compute average speed in m/s and km/h.

lessons.title: Units of Speed: m/s Meets km/h
lessons.focus: Conversion practice; reading boda speedometer; estimating matatu speed between kilometre markers.
lessons.advanced: Show 10 m/s = 36 km/h by chain conversion; which unit suits walking, which suits highways?

lessons.title: Average vs Instantaneous Speed
lessons.focus: Market journey with stops: total distance over total time vs reading at one instant; when each matters.
lessons.advanced: A journey: 2 km in 20 min, rest 10 min, 2 km in 30 min. Compute overall average speed and explain the rest's effect.

lessons.title: Velocity: Speed with a Direction
lessons.focus: Around-the-track walks; same speed, changing velocity in a circle; vectors drawn as arrows.
lessons.advanced: Two bodas at 40 km/h, one north one east: same speed, same velocity? Draw the velocity vectors.

lessons.title: Acceleration: Changing Speed
lessons.focus: Speeding up, slowing down, turning — all acceleration; boda leaving a stage; a = Δv/t introduced.
lessons.advanced: A matatu goes 0 to 15 m/s in 10 s: compute acceleration; what force ratio a=F/m does that imply per tonne?

lessons.title: Measuring Human Speed: The 20-Metre Dash
lessons.focus: Time classmates over 20 m; chart distribution; reaction error at the stopwatch; repeatable method.
lessons.advanced: Stopwatch operator has 0.2 s reaction on start and stop: estimate the speed error for a 3.5 s dash.

lessons.title: Distance–Time Graphs I: Plotting a Steady Walk
lessons.focus: Measure positions every 5 s on a marked course; plot; straight line for steady speed.
lessons.advanced: Extract speed from your graph gradient; compare with d/t from raw numbers — why agree?

lessons.title: Distance–Time Graphs II: Stops, Speed-ups and Returns
lessons.focus: Interpret stories from graph shapes; draw graph for a boda journey with a puncture stop; match graph to story cards.
lessons.advanced: Sketch the d–t graph for a ball thrown up and caught (distance from ground vs time) and defend the shape.

lessons.title: Speed–Time Graphs
lessons.focus: Gradient = acceleration; flat = steady; area under = distance (counting squares); plot the dash data.
lessons.advanced: From a v–t graph with constant acceleration 2 m/s² for 6 s, find distance travelled by area.

lessons.title: Build: A Ticker Timer from Simple Parts
lessons.focus: Hand-pulled paper tape under a clothespin-and-rubber 'tapper' metronome; dots record motion; analyze spacing.
materials: rubber band striker or felt pen
lessons.advanced: Dot spacing grows 2→4→6 mm at 5 beats/s: compute the three speeds and the acceleration.

lessons.title: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion
lessons.focus: Compare tape from steady pull vs falling mass pull; classify everyday motions; graph both.
lessons.advanced: Sketch d–t and v–t for uniform and for accelerating motion: four panels, labelled.

lessons.title: Motion of Vehicles: Odometers, Speedometers and Limits
lessons.focus: How speedo/odometer work (wheel rotations × circumference); why speed limits exist; NTSA context.
lessons.advanced: Wheel circumference 2.1 m turns 3 times per second: compute road speed in km/h.

lessons.title: Relative Motion: Passing and Being Passed
lessons.focus: Two walking students pass each other; speeds add/subtract; boat on flowing river stories.
lessons.advanced: Boat does 3 m/s on a river flowing 1 m/s: find effective speeds upstream and downstream and round-trip time for 600 m legs.

lessons.title: Reaction Time: The Ruler-Drop Test
lessons.focus: Catch a dropped ruler between fingers; distance fallen → reaction time via d=½gt²; chart the class.
lessons.advanced: Convert an 18 cm catch into reaction time using d=½gt² (g=10): show the working.

lessons.title: Thinking and Braking Distance
lessons.focus: Reaction distance + braking distance = stopping distance; toy-car crash demo; why tailgating kills.
lessons.advanced: At 20 m/s with 0.7 s reaction and 4 m/s² braking deceleration: compute total stopping distance.

lessons.title: Acceleration Lab: Toy Car on a Ramp
lessons.focus: Time car over measured ramp sections at different slopes; steeper → greater acceleration; graph results.
lessons.advanced: Using v²=2as with your measured time and distance, estimate acceleration on the steepest slope.

lessons.title: Rolling Down Ramps: Bottles, Balls and Cylinders
lessons.focus: Race solid ball vs bottle of water vs empty bottle; rolling is slower than sliding without friction would suggest — rotation teaser.
lessons.advanced: Explain using energy sharing between translation and rotation why the filled bottle and ball finish differently.

lessons.title: Deceleration: Slowing Down Is Acceleration Too
lessons.focus: Ball rolling out on grass; swing dying down; sign conventions for ±acceleration.
lessons.advanced: A ball enters grass at 4 m/s and stops in 2.5 m: find deceleration from v²=u²+2as.

lessons.title: Circular Motion Preview: Speed Constant, Velocity Changing
lessons.focus: Swing a stone on string; constant speed but changing direction means acceleration toward centre (deep dive Unit 10).
lessons.advanced: Argue why 'no acceleration at constant speed' fails for circular motion, using velocity vectors.

lessons.title: Project: Graph Your Journey to School
lessons.focus: Record times at landmarks on the way to school; draw d–t graph; find fastest/slowest legs; present.
lessons.advanced: Estimate uncertainty: phone-clock times ±30 s over 8 min legs — what speed uncertainty results?

lessons.title: Estimating Speed Without Instruments
lessons.focus: Calibrated pacing (your stride length), counting seconds by chant, kilometre markers; field estimates of boda speeds.
lessons.advanced: Design a zero-instrument speed survey for your road with ±20% accuracy; describe validation.

lessons.title: Motion of Animals: Cheetahs, Goats and Us
lessons.focus: Gaits and speeds; why cheetah spine flexes; ostrich vs human stride; timing a goat across the field.
lessons.advanced: Cheetah: 30 m/s for 15 s max; prey 20 m/s with 100 m head start — does the cheetah catch it? Show working.

lessons.title: Build: A Two-Gate Speed Trap for Toy Cars
lessons.focus: Two chalk gates + stopwatch (or clap-echo timing); test car designs down a ramp; class leaderboard.
lessons.advanced: Gate spacing 1.0 m, reaction error 0.15 s: which car speeds can you trust to two significant figures?

lessons.title: Unit Review: Motion Field Day
lessons.focus: Stations: dash timing, graph reading, reaction test, relative-motion demo; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Write one higher-order motion question (graph interpretation) with full marking scheme for the quiz.

units.title: Gravity, Falling Bodies & Projectiles
units.intro: From Galileo to water rockets: falling, terminal velocity and projectile range, measured in the school field.

lessons.title: The Story of Gravity: Aristotle, Galileo, Newton
lessons.focus: Ideas through history; Leaning Tower thought experiment; hammer-and-feather on the Moon (video or story).
lessons.advanced: Explain Galileo's chained-balls argument against 'heavier falls faster'.

lessons.title: Do Heavy Things Fall Faster? A Fair Test
lessons.focus: Drop stone vs flat paper, then crumpled paper; air resistance confound revealed; same-height release method.
lessons.advanced: Design the test so mass differs but shape does not (bottle + water levels); predict the outcome.

lessons.title: Free Fall and the Acceleration g
lessons.focus: g ≈ 10 m/s² meaning: speed grows 10 m/s each second; velocity table for 0-4 s of fall.
lessons.advanced: Compute speed and distance fallen at t=1,2,3 s using v=gt and d=½gt²; tabulate.

lessons.title: Measuring g: The Pendulum Promise
lessons.focus: Swing period depends on length not mass; preview T=2π√(L/g); plan the experiment (full method in Unit 11).
lessons.advanced: Rearrange T=2π√(L/g) to make g the subject; state what you'll plot.

lessons.title: Measuring g: The Two-Metre Drop
lessons.focus: Drop ball from measured 2 m; three timers average; compute g from d=½gt²; discuss error honestly.
lessons.advanced: Measured time 0.70 s for 2.0 m: compute g, percentage error vs 9.8, and list three error sources ranked.

lessons.title: Terminal Velocity: When Falling Stops Speeding Up
lessons.focus: Drag grows with speed until it balances weight; seeds, raindrops, parachutes; why an ant survives any fall.
lessons.advanced: Use surface-area-to-weight scaling to explain why big animals can't survive falls that insects shrug off.

lessons.title: Designing for Air: Parachute Science
lessons.focus: Canopy area vs fall speed; drop plastic-bag parachutes with stone payload; measure fall time vs area.
lessons.advanced: Plot fall time vs canopy area; fit a trend and extrapolate the area for a 60 kg person (order-of-magnitude).

lessons.title: Egg Drop Challenge I: Design and Build
lessons.focus: Protect a raw egg dropped 3 m using grass, paper, maize cobs, bags; impulse and crumple reasoning before building.
lessons.advanced: Justify your design with impulse: longer stopping time → smaller force (F=Δp/Δt preview).

lessons.title: Egg Drop Challenge II: Test and Autopsy
lessons.focus: Drop from ladder/veranda; inspect damage; correlate failure with design; improve and retest.
lessons.advanced: Estimate impact speed from 3 m (v=√(2gh)); then force for a 0.05 s stop on a 60 g egg.

lessons.title: Throwing Straight Up
lessons.focus: Ball up: slows at g, stops, returns at same speed (no air); time up = time down; catch height symmetry.
lessons.advanced: Total flight 2.4 s: compute launch speed and peak height using symmetry.

lessons.title: How High Did It Go? Energy Preview
lessons.focus: Estimate peak from flight time; KE→PE story; measure throw heights off a marked wall.
lessons.advanced: Equate ½mv²=mgh to show h=v²/2g; find launch speed for a 5 m mango-branch clearance.

lessons.title: Projectile Motion I: Sideways and Down Are Independent
lessons.focus: Roll ball off table while dropping another: same landing time; horizontal steady + vertical accelerates.
lessons.advanced: Ball leaves 1.25 m table at 3.0 m/s: compute flight time and range.

lessons.title: Projectile Motion II: Angle and Range
lessons.focus: Throw stones at measured angles; 45° wins (no air); 30° and 60° tie; javelin angle reality ~35°.
lessons.advanced: Explain with range formula R=v²sin2θ/g why 45° maximizes range; why do javelin throwers use less?

lessons.title: The Water Rocket Project I: Pressure and Design
lessons.focus: Bottle + water + air pressure = rocket; action-reaction and momentum preview; fin/nose design drawings.
lessons.advanced: Sketch forces on the rocket at launch: thrust, weight, drag; when is acceleration greatest?

lessons.title: The Water Rocket Project II: Build Day
lessons.focus: Construct fins, nose cone, payload bay; check symmetry and straight flight path; launcher safety briefing.
lessons.advanced: Compute centre of pressure vs centre of gravity positions; why must CG lead CP for stable flight?

lessons.title: The Water Rocket Project III: Launch and Measure
lessons.focus: Vary water fill (1/4, 1/3, 1/2) and launch angle; measure range and flight time; crown the champion with data.
lessons.advanced: From flight time and angle, estimate launch speed; explain the optimum fill fraction using mass vs impulse.

lessons.title: Physics of Kenyan Athletics
lessons.focus: Julius Yego's javelin angles, Eliud Kipchoge's pacing (steady speed = efficiency); analyze race splits from data cards.
lessons.advanced: Kipchoge: 42.195 km in 2:01:09 — compute average speed and per-km pace; compare with your dash.

lessons.title: Orbits and Satellites: Falling Around the Earth
lessons.focus: Throw harder and farther until you orbit; Kenya's space milestones (Uhuru-1, Taifa-1) and why satellites don't fall.
lessons.advanced: Explain weightlessness in orbit as continuous free fall, not absence of gravity.

lessons.title: The Coin and Feather Problem
lessons.focus: Attempt near-vacuum demo in a bottle with pump; failing that, reason from parachute data: without air, all fall together.
lessons.advanced: Write the argument that closes the case even if the demo is imperfect: what evidence settles it?

lessons.title: Unit Review: Gravity Games
lessons.focus: Stations: drop timing, parachute race, projectile range, egg-drop finals; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Combined problem: a stone thrown horizontally at 8 m/s from a 20 m cliff — time, range, impact speed.

units.title: Work, Energy & Power
units.intro: The physics of carrying water, splitting firewood and climbing hills: joules, watts and Kenya's energy story.

lessons.title: What 'Work' Means in Physics
lessons.focus: W = F × d in the force direction; carrying debe across yard (work) vs holding it still (no work).
lessons.advanced: You hold a 200 N load for 5 minutes: how much physics work is done, and why do your muscles tire anyway?

lessons.title: Calculating Work: Fetching Water and Lifting Loads
lessons.focus: Joules; compute work fetching a jerrican 20 m and lifting it 1.5 m onto a stand.
lessons.advanced: 200 N jerrican, 20 m level carry then 1.5 m lift: total work, and why the level carry counts only against friction.

lessons.title: When There Is No Work Done
lessons.focus: Pushing a wall, carrying at constant height (perpendicular force), orbiting: force without displacement does no work.
lessons.advanced: A satellite circles Earth under gravity: explain why gravity does zero work on a circular orbit.

lessons.title: Energy: The Ability to Do Work
lessons.focus: Survey of forms: chemical (food, firewood), kinetic, potential, elastic, heat, light, sound, electrical; energy hunt around school.
lessons.advanced: Classify ten school-compound energy stores and trace each back to the Sun where possible.

lessons.title: Kinetic Energy: Energy of Motion
lessons.focus: KE depends on mass and (especially) speed; rolling bottle vs rolling stone damage test on clay target.
lessons.advanced: Compute KE for a 1 kg bottle at 2 m/s vs 4 m/s: why does doubling speed quadruple the dent?

lessons.title: Gravitational Potential Energy: Tanks on Stands
lessons.focus: PE = mgh; water tank on a stand is an energy store; calculate PE of a 1000 L tank 3 m up.
lessons.advanced: A 1000 L tank (1000 kg) raised 3 m: compute stored PE and the fall energy per litre — why tanks stand high.

lessons.title: Elastic and Stored Energy
lessons.focus: Stretched rubber, drawn bow, bent stick, wound clock spring; store now, release later.
lessons.advanced: Estimate bow energy: average 30 N over 0.5 m draw — how fast could it launch a 30 g arrow ideally?

lessons.title: Energy Transformations I: Falling, Swinging, Shining
lessons.focus: Falling mango PE→KE; swing cycle; torch chemical→electrical→light; chain diagrams drawn for each.
lessons.advanced: Draw the full chain for a boda ride from food eaten at breakfast to kinetic energy, naming each store.

lessons.title: Energy Transformations II: The Jiko and the Body
lessons.focus: Charcoal chemical→heat→cooking; body food→motion+heat; efficiency preview (some energy always 'escapes').
lessons.advanced: A jiko uses 2 kg charcoal (≈30 MJ/kg) to deliver 6 MJ of cooking heat: compute efficiency.

lessons.title: Conservation of Energy: Nothing Lost, Everything Moved
lessons.focus: Pendulum returns to same height (minus a little); energy bookkeeping; where the 'lost' bit goes (heat, sound).
lessons.advanced: A 2 kg ball falls 5 m into a sand pit: account for all 100 J of energy at the end.

lessons.title: Where Does the Energy 'Go'? Friction and Heat
lessons.focus: Rub palms, feel brake blocks, bent wire heats; friction converts ordered motion to heat; lubrication saves energy.
lessons.advanced: A 60 kg student climbs 4 m of stairs (2400 J) but burns ~8000 J of food: explain the gap.

lessons.title: Measuring Your Own Power
lessons.focus: Timed stair climb with known mass and height: P = mgh/t in watts; compare classmates; compare to a 60 W bulb.
lessons.advanced: 50 kg student, 3 m stairs, 6 s: compute power; how long could a human power a 100 W TV?

lessons.title: Human Power vs Machine Power
lessons.focus: Person (~75 W sustained) vs boda engine (kW) vs posho mill vs water pump; why machines changed farming.
lessons.advanced: A 5 kW pump replaces how many workers lifting 20 L to 3 m every 90 s? Show working.

lessons.title: Food as Fuel: Kilojoules on the Plate
lessons.focus: Food labels in kJ; energy cost of walking, farming, studying; match meals to a day's work.
lessons.advanced: Ugali portion 1500 kJ: how many 3 m stair climbs (60 kg person) does it theoretically power?

lessons.title: Kenya's Energy Story: Firewood to Geothermal
lessons.focus: Firewood/charcoal, hydro (Seven Forks), geothermal (Olkaria), wind (Lake Turkana), solar home systems; mapping sources to uses.
lessons.advanced: Rank sources by renewability and reliability for a rural school; defend the ranking.

lessons.title: Efficiency: Useful Out Over Total In
lessons.focus: η = useful/total; traditional 3-stone fire vs improved jiko; why no machine beats 100%.
lessons.advanced: Improved jiko delivers 12 MJ from 40 MJ of charcoal; compute η and wood saved per week at 3 kg/day baseline.

lessons.title: Project: Home Energy Audit I — Collect the Data
lessons.focus: Survey home energy uses (cooking, lighting, phone charging, transport); estimate weekly energy by source.
lessons.advanced: Design the survey so answers are in kWh or MJ estimable units; justify your assumptions.

lessons.title: Project: Home Energy Audit II — Present the Savings Plan
lessons.focus: Tabulate class results; biggest savings opportunities; present a family energy-saving plan.
lessons.advanced: Convert charcoal kg/week to MJ and trees/year (≈25 MJ/kg charcoal, 6 kg wood per kg charcoal): make the case.

lessons.title: Teacher Demo: Burning a Groundnut to Heat Water
lessons.focus: Teacher-led: burn groundnut under a tin of water; estimate food energy from temperature rise; strict fire safety.
lessons.advanced: Water 50 g rises 20°C (4200 J/kg·°C → 4200 J): groundnut mass 0.5 g — compute J/g and compare with label ~24 kJ/g; why low?

lessons.title: The Work–Energy Link
lessons.focus: Work done on something becomes its energy: lift = mgh; drag = KE change; calculations tying Units 5.1-5.7 together.
lessons.advanced: A 1000 N force pushes a cart 15 m from rest; friction eats 5000 J: find final KE and speed for 200 kg cart.

lessons.title: Power Ratings: Reading Machines
lessons.focus: What '125 cc', '5 kW', '0.5 hp pump' mean; matching machine power to the job (pump head, load).
lessons.advanced: A 1 kW pump lifts water 8 m: compute maximum litres per minute at 60% efficiency.

lessons.title: Project: Rube Goldberg Energy Chain I — Design
lessons.focus: Design a 5-step energy chain reaction from junk (marble run → lever → pendulum → balloon pop...); draw energy-flow diagram.
materials: junk box: bottles, sticks, string, marbles, balloons, dominoes
lessons.advanced: Annotate the design with an energy store-and-transfer label at every step.

lessons.title: Project: Rube Goldberg Energy Chain II — Build and Run
lessons.focus: Build, test, debug; reliability counts; class run-through and judging.
lessons.advanced: Identify the weakest link energetically (where input barely exceeds threshold) and strengthen it.

lessons.title: Renewable vs Non-Renewable: The Charcoal Debate
lessons.focus: Structured debate: charcoal economy vs forests vs jobs; numbers on both sides; what sustainability means.
lessons.advanced: Kenya uses ~2.5 M tonnes charcoal/year: at 6 kg wood per kg, compute wood demand and discuss solutions numerically.

lessons.title: Units Mastery Day: Joules, Watts, Newtons
lessons.focus: Games and drills converting between N, J, W, m, kg, s; common confusions (W for work vs watt).
lessons.advanced: Derive the joule in base units (kg·m²/s²) and use it to check the units of KE = ½mv².

lessons.title: Unit Review: Energy Expo
lessons.focus: Teams run demo stations (power stairs, chains, jiko efficiency posters); unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Write the expo 'energy balance sheet' for one station showing inputs, useful outputs and losses.

units.title: Simple Machines
units.intro: Levers, pulleys, planes and gears — the six machines hiding inside every jembe, mkokoteni, bicycle and posho mill.

lessons.title: What Machines Do for Us
lessons.focus: Machines change force size, direction or speed; input/output; open the unit by lifting a heavy stone three ways.
lessons.advanced: A machine can't multiply work: explain the force-distance trade as conservation of energy.

lessons.title: Mechanical Advantage and Velocity Ratio
lessons.focus: MA = load/effort; VR = effort distance/load distance; efficiency = MA/VR; measure both on a simple lever.
lessons.advanced: Lever gives VR 4 but measured MA 3.2: compute efficiency and name the loss.

lessons.title: Levers Class 1: Seesaws, Crowbars and Pliers
lessons.focus: Fulcrum between effort and load; seesaw balancing different weights by distance; crowbar pulling nails.
lessons.advanced: 40 kg child balances 70 kg adult on a 3 m seesaw: find each distance from the fulcrum.

lessons.title: Levers Class 2: Wheelbarrows and Bottle Openers
lessons.focus: Load between fulcrum and effort; wheelbarrow physics; bottle opener and nutcracker anatomy.
lessons.advanced: Wheelbarrow: load 400 N at 0.4 m from wheel, handles at 1.2 m: find the lifting effort.

lessons.title: Levers Class 3: The Mwiko and the Human Arm
lessons.focus: Effort between fulcrum and load; mwiko stirring, fishing rod, tweezers; trading force for speed and reach.
lessons.advanced: Why did evolution pick class-3 arms? Discuss speed/force trade with biceps-at-4 cm numbers.

lessons.title: Moments: The Turning Force
lessons.focus: Moment = F × d from pivot; balance a ruler with unequal bottle-top piles by sliding positions.
lessons.advanced: 5 tops at 20 cm balance 8 tops at what distance? Then generalize: write the balance rule.

lessons.title: Law of Moments Lab: Weighing Without a Scale
lessons.focus: Balance an unknown stone against known water volumes on a ruler; compute the stone's mass.
lessons.advanced: Known 300 g at 18 cm balances unknown at 12 cm: compute unknown mass; list error sources.

lessons.title: Centre of Gravity: The Balance Point
lessons.focus: Balance a jembe and a broom on a finger; CG of regular vs irregular shapes; plumb line method with string+nut.
lessons.advanced: Use the plumb-line intersection method on a cut-out of Kenya: describe where the CG lands and why.

lessons.title: Levers in the Human Body
lessons.focus: Neck (class 1), calf raise (class 2), biceps (class 3); posture and load; why lifting with bent back hurts.
lessons.advanced: Head mass 5 kg tilted 30° shifts its line of action: explain the extra neck moment and 'text neck' fatigue.

lessons.title: Carrying Loads: The Physics of Head Portering
lessons.focus: Head carrying aligns load over spine; tump lines on foreheads; kiondo straps; energy studies show head loads are efficient.
lessons.advanced: Compare carrying 20 kg on head vs one shoulder: draw force lines and predict muscle effort differences.

lessons.title: Build: A Graduated Weighing Beam I
lessons.focus: Make a steelyard-style beam: fixed pan, sliding stone weight, notches calibrated with water (100 g = 100 mL).
lessons.advanced: Explain the sliding-weight principle with moments; why are the notches evenly spaced?

lessons.title: Build: A Graduated Weighing Beam II — Test and Certify
lessons.focus: Weigh five known items, plot error, adjust notches; 'certify' the beam with a class stamp.
lessons.advanced: Beam reads 5% high at 1 kg but exact at 500 g: diagnose a systematic cause and fix it.

lessons.title: The Wheel and Axle
lessons.focus: Mkokoteni wheel, doorknob, screwdriver, steering: big wheel turns small axle with multiplied force.
lessons.advanced: Windlass drum 4 cm radius, handle 40 cm: compute VR; how does that map to force on the rope?

lessons.title: Build: The Well Windlass
lessons.focus: Spool + crank + string + small bucket; lift 'water' from a desk-well; measure effort vs direct lift.
lessons.advanced: Measure effort with and without the crank; compute MA and discuss friction at the axle.

lessons.title: The Inclined Plane I: Ramp vs Lift
lessons.focus: Roll debe up a plank instead of lifting; same work, less force, more distance; measure with spring balance.
lessons.advanced: Ramp 3 m long, 1 m rise, 100 N load: ideal effort vs measured 45 N — efficiency?

lessons.title: The Inclined Plane II: Switchbacks and Loading Planks
lessons.focus: Hill paths zigzag; loading mkokoteni with planks; wheelchair ramps; measure effort vs ramp angle on a model.
lessons.advanced: Plot effort vs sin(angle) from your data: confirm the proportionality and extract the load's weight.

lessons.title: The Wedge: Pangas, Axes and Jembe Tips
lessons.focus: Two inclined planes back to back; splitting firewood; why thin sharp wedges need less force; sharpening as physics.
lessons.advanced: A wedge 10 cm long, 2 cm thick driven by 200 N: ideal splitting force? (VR = length/thickness.)

lessons.title: The Screw: A Spiral Inclined Plane
lessons.focus: Unwrap a paper triangle from a bottle thread; car screw jack lifting a vehicle; G-clamp force; wood screws vs nails.
lessons.advanced: Jack pitch 3 mm, handle 30 cm: compute VR per turn and ideal load for 200 N effort.

lessons.title: Pulleys I: The Fixed Pulley
lessons.focus: Flagpole and well pulley change direction only; build fixed pulley from a spool/wire hanger; MA = 1, comfort = high.
lessons.advanced: If a fixed pulley gives no force advantage, why do wells still use them? Three physical reasons.

lessons.title: Pulleys II: The Movable Pulley Halves the Effort
lessons.focus: One fixed + one movable; count supporting strands = ideal MA; measure real effort vs prediction.
lessons.advanced: Two-strand system lifts 100 N with measured 60 N: ideal effort, efficiency, and where 10 N went.

lessons.title: Block and Tackle: The Jua Kali Engine Hoist
lessons.focus: Chain blocks lifting engines; rig a 4-strand system; the long pull for a big lift; safety under suspended loads.
lessons.advanced: 4-strand tackle, load 800 N, efficiency 70%: effort required and rope pulled for a 0.5 m lift.

lessons.title: Pulley Lab: Effort vs Strand Count
lessons.focus: Systematically measure effort for 1,2,3,4 strands; plot effort vs 1/strands; discuss friction's growing share.
lessons.advanced: Fit your data to effort = W/(n·η): estimate η per strand and explain the downward trend.

lessons.title: Gears: Trading Speed for Force
lessons.focus: Bicycle gears; big cog slow-strong, small cog fast-weak; count teeth, compute ratios; drawgear on posho mill teaser.
lessons.advanced: Front 44 teeth, rear 11 vs 28: compute wheel turns per pedal turn and the climbing advantage ratio.

lessons.title: Belt Drives: Posho Mills and Sewing Machines
lessons.focus: Belt connects pulleys; crossed vs open belt direction; slipping as a safety feature; tension adjustment.
lessons.advanced: Driver 10 cm, driven 30 cm: compute speed ratio and torque ratio for the posho mill.

lessons.title: The Bicycle: A Machine Made of Machines I
lessons.focus: Identify lever (pedals, brakes), wheel-axle, gears, chain drive, bearings, screws on a real boda bicycle.
lessons.advanced: Trace the force path from foot to road, naming every machine and its MA contribution.

lessons.title: The Bicycle II: Measuring Its Advantages
lessons.focus: Count gear teeth, measure pedal-arm and wheel radii, compute real ratios; brake lever MA; present findings.
lessons.advanced: Combine pedal lever (0.17 m), chainring/cog ratio and wheel radius into one force multiplication number.

lessons.title: The Treadle Sewing Machine: Foot to Needle
lessons.focus: Treadle (lever) → crank → flywheel (rotation smoothed) → belt → needle; energy storage in the flywheel.
lessons.advanced: Explain how the flywheel's stored energy carries the mechanism past the 'dead spots' of each stitch cycle.

lessons.title: Design Challenge: A Machine for Our Village I
lessons.focus: Teams choose a real task (lifting water, shelling maize, pressing tiles); sketch using ≥3 simple machines; peer review.
lessons.advanced: Estimate the combined MA and efficiency of your design from component values.

lessons.title: Design Challenge II: Build and Demonstrate
lessons.focus: Build the chosen machine from jua kali scrap and school materials; demonstrate lifting/moving a real load.
lessons.advanced: Measure actual MA with a spring balance; compare with design prediction and explain the gap.

lessons.title: Why Machines Waste Energy
lessons.focus: Friction in axles and ropes; efficiency measured across the unit's builds; lubrication and alignment as cures.
lessons.advanced: Rank the class builds by efficiency and propose one modification each that raises η by ≥10%.

lessons.title: Maintenance Matters: Oiling, Tightening, Aligning
lessons.focus: Boda service schedule as physics: chain lube, brake pads, bearing play; write a maintenance card for a class build.
lessons.advanced: Quantify: a dry chain wastes ~5% of pedal energy — how many extra food kJ per 10 km ride?

lessons.title: Unit Review: Machine Fair
lessons.focus: Every build on show with student explainers; visitors operate each; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Prepare a 2-minute explainer for one machine: include MA, VR, efficiency and one safety rule.

units.title: Pressure & Fluids at Rest
units.intro: From the sharp panga to the village water tower: pressure in solids, liquids and air, with siphons and hydraulics built by hand.

lessons.title: What Is Pressure? Force Spread Over Area
lessons.focus: P = F/A; sharp nail pierces, blunt one doesn't; sitting on one stone vs a flat board; units N/m² (pascal).
lessons.advanced: Compute the pressure under a 50 N nail tip of 0.1 mm²; compare with a 500 N student on two feet (300 cm²).

lessons.title: Pressure in Daily Life: Sharp, Wide, Deep
lessons.focus: Panga edge vs spine, high heels in mud, wide tractor tyres, heavy lorries vs murram roads; hooves comparison.
lessons.advanced: Explain why wide tyres 'float' a tractor on soft soil using numbers: double area, halve pressure.

lessons.title: Calculating Pressure: Feet, Hooves and Jerricans
lessons.focus: Measure your foot area on squared paper; compute standing pressures; full jerrican on its base.
lessons.advanced: One foot vs two vs tiptoe: compute all three pressures and relate to sinking in mud.

lessons.title: Pressure in Liquids I: The Jerrican with Three Holes
lessons.focus: Holes at three heights jet different distances; deeper = more pressure; pressure acts in all directions.
lessons.advanced: Measure jet ranges vs depth; explain the shape of the relationship qualitatively.

lessons.title: Pressure in Liquids II: P = ρgh and Dam Walls
lessons.focus: Build P=ρgh from a water column's weight; dam walls thicker at the base (Masinga, Thwake); units check.
lessons.advanced: Compute pressure at 10 m depth (ρ=1000, g=10); what force on a 1 m² sluice gate at that depth?

lessons.title: Water Finds Its Level: Communicating Vessels
lessons.focus: Connected tubes settle level regardless of shape; teapot spout physics; spirit-level alternative.
lessons.advanced: Explain with P=ρgh why the levels must match, including for two different-width arms.

lessons.title: Build: The Hose Water Level (Fundi's Tool)
lessons.focus: Clear tube + water makes a long-distance level; mark two posts at identical height across a slope; test against a spirit level.
lessons.advanced: Why must there be no air bubble in the tube? Quantify the error a 5 cm bubble could cause.

lessons.title: Build: The U-Tube Manometer
lessons.focus: Bend tubing into a U; water levels measure small pressures; measure lung pressure by gentle blowing; read mm of water.
lessons.advanced: Convert a 300 mm water difference into pascals using P=ρgh.

lessons.title: Air Has Weight: Atmospheric Pressure Exists
lessons.focus: Teacher demo: crush a tin with steam + cold water; rubber suckers stick; air presses ~100 kPa at sea level.
lessons.advanced: Atmospheric pressure ≈ 101 kPa: force on a 10 cm² tin lid? Why aren't we crushed?

lessons.title: Using Air Pressure: Straws, Syringes and Suckers
lessons.focus: Drinking through a straw is the atmosphere pushing; syringe filling; hook suckers; 'suction' is a myth — pressure difference is real.
lessons.advanced: Explain the maximum straw-lift height from P=ρgh with atmospheric pressure (≈10 m of water).

lessons.title: Altitude and Air Pressure: From the Coast to the Highlands
lessons.focus: Ears pop on the escarpment; sealed bottles swell when travelling down; boiling point drops in the highlands (cooking time!).
lessons.advanced: Nairobi ≈ 1660 m, ~84 kPa: why does ugali cooking take longer there? Link pressure to boiling point.

lessons.title: Build: A Bottle Barometer for Weather Watching
lessons.focus: Inverted bottle neck in water jar; falling water = rising pressure; keep a two-week weather log against observations.
lessons.advanced: Explain why temperature changes can fool a bottle barometer; propose a correction routine.

lessons.title: Pascal's Principle: Pressure Travels Through Fluids
lessons.focus: Squeeze a sealed bottle, water jets from all holes equally; pressure applied to enclosed fluid transmits undiminished.
lessons.advanced: State Pascal's principle and use it to derive the hydraulic force multiplication F2=F1·A2/A1.

lessons.title: Hydraulic Machines I: The Syringe Lift
lessons.focus: Two syringes + tube of water: small plunger lifts heavy load on big plunger; measure the multiplication.
lessons.advanced: Plungers 1 cm² and 10 cm²: ideal MA, and the distance trade when small plunger moves 10 cm.

lessons.title: Hydraulic Machines II: Brakes, Presses and Excavators
lessons.focus: Car brake circuits, jua kali press, excavator arms; why fluid not air (incompressibility); bleeding brakes story.
lessons.advanced: Explain why an air bubble in a brake line makes the pedal 'spongy' and dangerous.

lessons.title: Build: The Hydraulic Lift Challenge I
lessons.focus: Team build: syringe-and-tube lift raising a stone platform; document design choices.
lessons.advanced: Predict the maximum load from plunger areas and your measured push force.

lessons.title: Build: The Hydraulic Lift Challenge II — Test and Measure
lessons.focus: Competition: heaviest load lifted 2 cm; compute MA and efficiency; leak post-mortems.
lessons.advanced: Your lift achieved MA 6 vs ideal 10: name two loss mechanisms and one fix each.

lessons.title: Pressure in Gases: Particles on the Attack
lessons.focus: Pump a ball/tyre and feel it firm up; particles bombarding walls; pressure rises when volume shrinks (qualitative).
lessons.advanced: Use particle collisions to explain why a sealed balloon shrinks in cold water.

lessons.title: Squeezing Air: A Qualitative Boyle's Law
lessons.focus: Seal a syringe and push: volume halves, push-back roughly doubles; graphs for the older students.
lessons.advanced: Take volume vs pressure readings with stacked weights; test P·V ≈ constant from your data.

lessons.title: Levers vs Hydraulics: Choosing a Force Multiplier
lessons.focus: Compare builds from Units 6 and 7: which multiplier for which job (precision, distance, dirt, maintenance).
lessons.advanced: Write a selection guide: lifting 1 tonne 0.5 m in a muddy garage — lever, tackle or hydraulic? Justify.

lessons.title: Why Water Tanks Stand Tall: Gravity Supply
lessons.focus: Head of water creates pressure; village gravity schemes from hill springs; compute the pressure of a 10 m standpipe.
lessons.advanced: Tap is 15 m below tank surface: pressure in kPa and the jet speed estimate (Torricelli v=√2gh) at the tap.

lessons.title: Siphon Theory: The River That Climbs a Hill
lessons.focus: How a siphon starts and runs; the rising leg works because atmosphere pushes; the falling leg pulls; height limits.
lessons.advanced: Explain with pressures at the crest why the lift leg cannot exceed ~10 m for water.

lessons.title: Siphon Practice I: Starting Methods
lessons.focus: Fill-tube-first method, pump-start, and safe mouth-start with clean water only; empty a jerrican to a lower basin.
lessons.advanced: Why does the siphon stop when the upper end sucks air? Describe the pressure chain breaking.

lessons.title: Siphon Practice II: Cisterns, Furrows and Ponds
lessons.focus: Toilet cistern siphon anatomy; draining a flooded trench; siphon to move water over a bund into furrows.
lessons.advanced: Compare siphon vs pump for emptying a pit 1 m deep over a 2 m bund: which is cheaper and why?

lessons.title: Pressure Safety: Cookers, Cylinders and Sealed Tins
lessons.focus: Pressure cooker valve physics; never heat sealed containers; gas cylinder care; borehole cap dangers.
lessons.advanced: Cooker at 200 kPa absolute on a 6 cm diameter lid: compute the clamping force the valve system handles.

lessons.title: Measuring Big Pressures: Pumps and Tyre Gauges
lessons.focus: Bicycle pump anatomy (valve!); tyre gauge reads kPa/psi; pump up and measure; why small pumps make big pressures.
lessons.advanced: Pump barrel 3 cm bore, 200 N effort: compute the pressure it can generate in kPa and psi (1 psi ≈ 6.9 kPa).

lessons.title: Build: The Cartesian Diver
lessons.focus: Dropper in a capped bottle: squeeze and it dives; buoyancy + pressure + gas compressibility in one toy.
lessons.advanced: Explain the dive using air-pocket compression changing average density; predict behavior at constant squeeze.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Pressure Lab Stations
lessons.focus: Stations: jerrican jets, manometer, syringe lift, siphon, diver; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Capstone-style question: design a system to water a garden 20 m below a tank, with flow control; mark scheme included.

units.title: Fluids in Motion, Siphons & Pumps
units.intro: Flow, Bernoulli, valves and the pumps that move Kenya's water — from the Afridev hand pump to the sump pump and the ram pump.

lessons.title: Measuring Flow: Litres per Second
lessons.focus: Time a jerrican filling at the tap; flow rate = volume/time; compare taps, trickles and the river (float method teaser).
lessons.advanced: A 20 L jerrican fills in 45 s: flow rate in L/s and L/hour; how long to fill a 1000 L tank?

lessons.title: Narrow Pipe, Faster Flow: Continuity
lessons.focus: Thumb over the hose speeds the jet; rivers quicken at narrows; A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ for incompressible flow.
lessons.advanced: Pipe narrows from 5 cm to 2 cm diameter: compute the speed-up factor from areas.

lessons.title: The Bernoulli Surprise I: Papers That Kiss
lessons.focus: Blow between two hanging papers — they come together; fast air = lower pressure; ball levitating in a jet.
lessons.advanced: Use Bernoulli's equation qualitatively to rank pressures at three points in a narrowing pipe.

lessons.title: The Bernoulli Surprise II: Roofs, Sprays and Dust Devils
lessons.focus: Why mabati roofs lift in storms; perfume/pesticide atomizers; wind over a chimney draws smoke; safe-roof discussion.
lessons.advanced: Estimate uplift force: wind 20 m/s over a 40 m² roof using ΔP≈½ρv² (ρ=1.2).

lessons.title: Curve Balls: The Magnus Effect
lessons.focus: Football free kicks bend; throw a bottle with spin and watch it drift; spin drags air and makes a pressure difference.
lessons.advanced: Explain top-spin vs back-spin effects on flight using pressure differences.

lessons.title: Pumps: Moving Water Against Gravity
lessons.focus: Survey: hand pumps, diesel pumps, electric pumps, solar pumps across Kenya; what all pumps share (a moving seal).
lessons.advanced: Rank hand, diesel and solar pumps for a 20-family village by lifetime cost and reliability; defend with assumptions.

lessons.title: Lift Pumps: The Afridev and the 10-Metre Limit
lessons.focus: Hand pump anatomy: piston, valves, the atmosphere does the lifting; why suction fails beyond ~10 m.
lessons.advanced: Derive the max suction lift from P=ρgh with atmospheric pressure; why is practical lift only ~7 m?

lessons.title: Force Pumps: Pushing Water Upward
lessons.focus: Force pump pushes water above the pump itself; bicycle pump as air force-pump; pressure washer idea.
lessons.advanced: Compare lift vs force pump for raising water 25 m from a deep well: which and why?

lessons.title: Centrifugal Pumps: Spinning Water Outward
lessons.focus: Bucket on a string swung = water thrown outward; impeller idea; most electric borehole pumps are centrifugal.
lessons.advanced: Explain why a centrifugal pump must be primed but a positive-displacement pump self-primes.

lessons.title: The Sump Pump: Draining the Pit
lessons.focus: Flooded basements and pit latrines in Nairobi rains; float switch rises with water; check valve stops backflow; submersible vs pedestal.
lessons.advanced: Design the float-switch geometry: at what water level should the pump cut in and out, and why a gap between them?

lessons.title: Project: The Siphon Garden System I — Design
lessons.focus: Overhead tank → tube over the bund → furrows below; plan heights, tube routing, distribution points for a school garden.
lessons.advanced: Compute available head and predict flow for a 15 mm tube using Torricelli reasoning.

lessons.title: Project: The Siphon Garden System II — Build and Test
lessons.focus: Install tubes, start siphons safely, measure flow at each outlet; map flow vs head difference.
lessons.advanced: Plot flow vs head; why does real flow fall below the √2gh ideal? (Friction in the tube.)

lessons.title: Project: The Siphon Garden System III — Troubleshoot and Maintain
lessons.focus: Air leaks, blockages, algae; priming ritual; seasonal checklist; handover document for next year's class.
lessons.advanced: Write the fault tree: no flow → (air in crest? inlet uncovered? outlet above inlet?) with a test for each branch.

lessons.title: Valves: The Heart of Every Pump
lessons.focus: One-way flap valves from inner-tube rubber; watch one work on a clear tube; heart valves analogy; check valves in pumps.
lessons.advanced: Explain the pumping cycle as two valves opening alternately; what failure does a leaking inlet valve cause?

lessons.title: Build: A Hand Diaphragm Pump I
lessons.focus: Bottle + rubber diaphragm + two flap valves = working lift pump; assemble the pump head.
lessons.advanced: Estimate litres per stroke from diaphragm displacement; predict strokes per jerrican.

lessons.title: Build: A Hand Diaphragm Pump II — Performance Test
lessons.focus: Measure L/min at lift heights 0.5/1.0/1.5 m; graph performance; compare against a commercial pump spec.
lessons.advanced: Fit flow vs height trend; compute the pump's useful power at 1 m lift (P=ρgQh).

lessons.title: The Hydraulic Ram: Water That Pumps Itself
lessons.focus: Water hammer: stop a flowing column suddenly and pressure spikes; ram pumps lift a fraction high using only falling water; Kenyan hillside sites.
lessons.advanced: Explain the ram cycle (waste valve, delivery valve, air chamber) as momentum becoming pressure.

lessons.title: Teacher-Led Build: A Mini Ram Pump I
lessons.focus: Bottle air-chamber + two flap valves + drive pipe; teacher-led assembly of a demonstration ram.
lessons.advanced: Compute the drive head and delivery head of your rig; estimate the efficiency fraction Q·H/(q·h).

lessons.title: Teacher-Led Build: A Mini Ram Pump II — Tuning
lessons.focus: Tune waste-valve weight and air chamber; measure delivery per minute; discuss real installations (AidFoundation/ram pump groups).
lessons.advanced: Why does the air chamber smooth the delivery flow? Quantify with your pulsation count before/after.

lessons.title: Irrigation Physics: Drip, Furrow and Sprinkler
lessons.focus: Drip needs little pressure, sprinkler lots; gravity drip kits from a raised jerrican; water budgeting for dry seasons.
lessons.advanced: A bed needs 5 mm of water on 4 m² daily: compute litres/day and the drip-line hours at your measured rate.

lessons.title: Rivers, Bridges and Floods: Motion at Large Scale
lessons.focus: Fast water undermines bridge piers (scour); flood energy; gabions and check dams slow water; Kenyan flood examples.
lessons.advanced: Explain with KE∝v² why doubling flood speed quadruples its destructive energy per unit mass.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Water Works Expo
lessons.focus: All pumps and the siphon garden running; student engineers explain; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Write the expo quiz's hard question: a two-valve pump fault diagnosis with full reasoning.

units.title: Buoyancy & Floating
units.intro: Why the sufuria floats but the nail sinks: Archimedes with jerricans, clay boats, hydrometers and lake safety.

lessons.title: Sink or Float? The Prediction Game
lessons.focus: Predict then test twenty local objects (nail, coin, maize cob, charcoal, bottle top, mango seed, stone, leaf, wax, wire); tabulate surprises.
lessons.advanced: From the class table, state the rule that beats 'heavy things sink' with three counter-examples.

lessons.title: Density Decides: Wood, Stone and Steel
lessons.focus: Average density vs water (1000 kg/m³) predicts floating; the steel nail sinks but the steel sufuria floats — shape matters.
lessons.advanced: A hollow steel ball's average density is 600 kg/m³: what fraction of its volume is air?

lessons.title: Upthrust: Water Pushes Back
lessons.focus: Weigh a stone in air, then in water: apparent weight drops; upthrust measured with a spring balance.
lessons.advanced: Stone: 2.5 N in air, 1.5 N in water: upthrust, displaced water weight, and the stone's volume.

lessons.title: Archimedes' Principle
lessons.focus: Upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid; verify by collecting overflow from the eureka can and weighing it.
lessons.advanced: Show a floating object's displaced weight equals its own weight — derive the floating condition.

lessons.title: The Eureka Can Lab: Volume by Overflow
lessons.focus: Measure irregular volumes precisely by overflow; link displacement to Unit 1 density measurements.
lessons.advanced: An object displaces 120 mL and weighs 3.0 N in air: density, and will it float?

lessons.title: Why Ships Float: Shape Beats Material
lessons.focus: Same clay ball sinks, same clay as a bowl floats; average density includes the hollow; dhow and ferry examples.
lessons.advanced: Compute the minimum hollow fraction for a steel hull (ρ=7800) to float; why do ships sink when swamped?

lessons.title: Clay Boat Challenge I: Design for Cargo
lessons.focus: Design a clay hull to carry bottle-top cargo; predict capacity from displaced volume.
lessons.advanced: Boat clay mass 200 g; hull displaces 800 cm³ at gunwale: maximum safe cargo in grams?

lessons.title: Clay Boat Challenge II: Load Test and Stability
lessons.focus: Load to sinking; record capacity; stability: wide beams vs tall cargo; freeboard concept.
lessons.advanced: Explain via centre of gravity vs centre of buoyancy why top-heavy boats capsize.

lessons.title: The Hydrometer: A Floater That Measures
lessons.focus: Floating depth reveals density; milk purity testing at the dairy; battery acid testers; salinity for fish farmers.
lessons.advanced: Why does the hydrometer sink deeper in less-dense liquid? Derive the depth-density relation for a uniform stick.

lessons.title: Build: A Pencil Hydrometer
lessons.focus: Weight a pencil with clay, float it, mark fresh-water line, calibrate with salt solutions; test unknowns.
lessons.advanced: Calibrate marks at 1.00, 1.05, 1.10 g/cm³: describe how you verified each.

lessons.title: Layers of Liquid: The Egg in Salt Water
lessons.focus: Egg sinks in fresh, floats in strong salt solution; density columns (salty below fresh, carefully poured).
lessons.advanced: Compute the salt concentration needed for neutral buoyancy of an egg (ρ≈1.05 g/cm³) — method and caveats.

lessons.title: Submarines and Swim Bladders
lessons.focus: Fish adjust a gas bladder; submarines flood and blow ballast tanks; Cartesian diver (Unit 7) as the working model.
lessons.advanced: A submarine at constant depth takes on water: what must happen to its ballast and why?

lessons.title: Rafts, Canoes and Ferries of Kenya
lessons.focus: Banana-stem and ambatch rafts, dugout canoes on Lake Victoria, ferries at Likoni; buoyancy calculations for safe loading.
lessons.advanced: Raft of 10 logs, each 40 L displacement, total mass 150 kg: safe passenger load in kg?

lessons.title: Life Jackets and Water Safety
lessons.focus: How a life jacket adds buoyancy without adding weight; cold water and panic; community water-safety campaign design.
lessons.advanced: A 70 kg person (body density ≈ 1.02) needs how much extra displaced volume to float face-up? Show working.

lessons.title: Plimsoll Lines: Loading Marks on Ships
lessons.focus: Load lines for fresh vs salt water; mark your clay boat's Plimsoll line; overloading tragedies discussion.
lessons.advanced: A ship moves from sea (1.025) to fresh water (1.000): by what percentage does displaced volume change?

lessons.title: Hot Air Rises: Buoyancy in Gases
lessons.focus: Smoke rises; teacher demo tissue hot-air balloon; air has density too; bridge to thermal physics (Unit on temperature in CBE 1.4).
lessons.advanced: Hot air at 0.9 kg/m³ in a 1 m³ balloon, outside 1.2: net lift force in newtons; payload in grams.

lessons.title: Design Project: A Floating Garden or Fish Cage
lessons.focus: Design a buoyant platform for vegetables (jerricans under bamboo); compute buoyancy budget; present.
lessons.advanced: Full buoyancy budget: platform + soil + water + crop vs total displacement, with 30% safety margin.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Regatta Day
lessons.focus: Clay-boat races, hydrometer readings, buoyancy puzzle stations; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Championship problem: design a boat to carry 500 g in salt water with minimal clay — show the displacement math.

units.title: Circular & Rotational Motion
units.intro: Spinning stones, cornering bodas, flywheels and grinding mills: the physics of going round.

lessons.title: Motion in Circles: Everywhere You Look
lessons.focus: Wheels, mills, merry-go-rounds, fans, steering; distinguish rotation (spinning) from revolution (orbiting).
lessons.advanced: Give three Kenyan machines using each: rotation about a fixed axle vs revolution around an external centre.

lessons.title: What Keeps It Circling? The Inward Pull
lessons.focus: Swing a soft ball on a string; cut the string mentally: ball flies off tangent; centripetal force is a requirement, not a new force.
lessons.advanced: A 0.5 kg ball at 3 m/s on a 1 m string: compute the centripetal force (F=mv²/r) and compare with its weight.

lessons.title: Sources of Centripetal Force
lessons.focus: String tension, tyre friction in cornering, gravity for the Moon, banked-track normal force; identify the provider in five cases.
lessons.advanced: Boda cornering at 10 m/s on radius 15 m: required friction force for 150 kg total; what happens on wet murram?

lessons.title: The Bucket of Water Overhead
lessons.focus: Teacher-led swing of a small water bucket overhead; why the water stays in; speed threshold felt at the shoulder.
lessons.advanced: Minimum speed at the top: set centripetal acceleration ≥ g; compute v_min for a 1 m arm.

lessons.title: Speed Around the Circle: v = 2πr/T
lessons.focus: Measure a merry-go-round or spinning wheel: count rotations, time them, compute rim speed.
lessons.advanced: Rim at 1.2 m radius turns once per 2.5 s: rim speed and centripetal acceleration (a=v²/r).

lessons.title: Why You Feel Flung Outward
lessons.focus: Inertia carries you straight while the vehicle turns; 'centrifugal force' as a felt effect; soap in the spinning basin demo.
lessons.advanced: Explain the sliding-passenger sensation from the ground frame without inventing a new force.

lessons.title: Leaning Bodas and Banked Corners
lessons.focus: Riders lean into corners; banked velodromes and railway curves; lean angle relates speed and radius.
lessons.advanced: tanθ = v²/(rg): compute the lean angle for 8 m/s on a 10 m radius corner.

lessons.title: The Herder's Sling: Release at the Right Moment
lessons.focus: Whirl a sling with a soft clay ball; release timing controls direction; safety protocols in an open field.
lessons.advanced: Release at height 1.5 m, speed 15 m/s horizontal: compute range and explain the best release point in the circle.

lessons.title: Grinding and Milling: Rotation at Work
lessons.focus: Kinu grinding stone, posho mill burrs; big slow wheels grind with torque; visit or diagram a posho mill's drivetrain.
lessons.advanced: Mill burr at 20 cm radius, 600 rpm: compute rim speed; why is high rim speed good for grinding?

lessons.title: Flywheels: Storing Rotation
lessons.focus: Posho mill and treadle wheels keep spinning through the dead spots; spin a heavy wheel and feel the persistence.
lessons.advanced: Explain with rotational inertia why mass at the rim stores more energy than mass at the hub.

lessons.title: Balancing a Wheel
lessons.focus: Unbalanced wheel shakes; find the heavy spot on a free bicycle wheel; add clay counterweight until smooth.
lessons.advanced: Explain why imbalance force grows with v² and what that means for a boda at speed.

lessons.title: The Gyroscope Effect: Spinning Means Stability
lessons.focus: Spinning tops, rolling coins, moving bicycles stay upright; stationary bike falls over; precession teaser on a swivel stool.
lessons.advanced: Use angular momentum direction-stability to explain why a rolling bicycle self-corrects small leans.

lessons.title: Rolling: Rotation Plus Translation
lessons.focus: A rolling wheel's rim point touching ground is momentarily still; rolling vs dragging a debe measured with a spring balance.
lessons.advanced: Mark the wheel contact point's path (cycloid) from chalk dots; argue why rolling friction is small.

lessons.title: Ball Bearings: Rolling Between Surfaces
lessons.focus: Open a boda hub (or diagram): balls roll instead of metals sliding; races, cages, grease; failure signs.
lessons.advanced: Estimate friction reduction sliding→rolling from hub temperatures felt before/after service; design a better test.

lessons.title: Axles and Torque: The Long Spanner Rule
lessons.focus: Long spanner loosens stubborn nuts; wheel radius vs axle radius; torque = F × r introduced.
lessons.advanced: 300 N on a 30 cm spanner vs 15 cm: compute both torques; why do mechanics add a pipe?

lessons.title: Build: A Bottle-Top Carousel
lessons.focus: Wire axle through a bottle-cap platform with bead seats; spin and measure period vs radius of beads.
lessons.advanced: Beads at 5 cm vs 10 cm: compare their speeds for the same spin rate; where do they fly off first and why?

lessons.title: Spinning Eggs: Raw vs Boiled
lessons.focus: Boiled spins long, raw wobbles out — liquid inside lags; moment-of-inertia teaser; stop-and-release trick.
lessons.advanced: Explain the stop-and-release restart of the raw egg using internal fluid motion and inertia.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Circle Circus
lessons.focus: Stations: sling range, carousel timing, balance a wheel, egg test; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Design a safe playground roundabout speed limit using a=v²/r and justify your numbers.

units.title: Oscillations & Pendulums
units.intro: Swings, springs and shocks: the repeating motions that measure time and smooth our rides.

lessons.title: Back and Forth: The World Oscillates
lessons.focus: Swings, pendulums, springs, branches, guitar strings; define cycle, period, frequency, amplitude.
lessons.advanced: A pendulum makes 20 cycles in 25 s: compute period and frequency with units.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Pendulum
lessons.focus: Bob, string, pivot; equilibrium position; restoring force grows with displacement; energy sloshes PE↔KE.
lessons.advanced: Sketch force arrows at both extremes and at the bottom; where is speed greatest and why?

lessons.title: Timing a Pendulum Properly
lessons.focus: Time 10 swings and divide; start at 'zero' at the fastest point; why single-swing timing lies.
lessons.advanced: Ten swings: 19.8, 20.2, 20.0 s. Give period with uncertainty and explain the 10-swing gain.

lessons.title: What Affects the Period? Test: Mass
lessons.focus: Same length, stone vs wooden bob: no change; fair-test discipline; Galileo's cathedral story.
lessons.advanced: Explain mass-independence using both F=ma and the PE↔KE exchange.

lessons.title: What Affects the Period? Test: Amplitude
lessons.focus: Small vs large swings: nearly equal (small-angle magic); where it breaks down (>30°).
lessons.advanced: Measure period at 10°, 30°, 60°: quantify the breakdown and explain the small-angle approximation.

lessons.title: What Affects the Period? Test: Length — The One That Matters
lessons.focus: Vary length 20–100 cm; period grows; collect the class dataset for the graph lesson.
lessons.advanced: Predict the period at 25 cm given 1.0 s at 100 cm, using T∝√L.

lessons.title: The Pendulum Graph: T² Against L
lessons.focus: Plot T² vs L: a straight line through origin; gradient = 4π²/g; compute g from your own graph.
lessons.advanced: Full computation: gradient 0.040 s²/cm → g in m/s²; compare with your Unit 4 drop result.

lessons.title: Measuring g Precisely: Pendulum vs Drop
lessons.focus: Compare pendulum and drop methods side by side; which is more accurate and why; repeatability.
lessons.advanced: Write an error budget for both methods; recommend the school-standard procedure.

lessons.title: Build: The One-Second Pendulum Clock I
lessons.focus: Build a stand and pendulum; target T=1.00 s; compute the needed length (≈25 cm) then approach it by tuning.
lessons.advanced: Use T=2π√(L/g) to predict L for T=1.000 s at g=9.8; compare with your tuned result.

lessons.title: Build: The One-Second Pendulum Clock II — Calibrate
lessons.focus: Adjust length against a clock over 5 minutes; temperature and wind effects; log drift; name your clock.
lessons.advanced: Clock gains 2 s per 10 min: compute the length correction needed, with direction.

lessons.title: How to Pump a Swing Higher
lessons.focus: Standing-squatting timing pumps energy in; parametric pumping felt on a playground swing; timing is everything.
lessons.advanced: Explain pumping as changing effective length twice per cycle; where does the added energy come from?

lessons.title: Resonance: Small Pushes, Big Swings
lessons.focus: Push at the natural frequency; shaky bridge stories, wine-glass legend, boda bouncing on corrugations; damping as the cure.
materials: two pendulums on a shared string
lessons.advanced: Two coupled pendulums: explain energy transfer when lengths match, and detuning when they don't.

lessons.title: Damping: The Shock Absorber's Job
lessons.focus: Swings stop by air + friction; test a mass on rubber with and without a card damper; boda shocks bounce-test.
lessons.advanced: A bounce-test corner settles in 1.5 vs 4 cycles after shock service: explain what changed energetically.

lessons.title: Springs Oscillate Too: Mass on a Rubber Strip
lessons.focus: Period vs hanging mass measured; heavier = slower here (unlike pendulum); T∝√m pattern.
lessons.advanced: Plot T² vs m; use the gradient with T=2π√(m/k) to extract your strip's spring constant k.

lessons.title: Build: A Stick Metronome
lessons.focus: Inverted pendulum with sliding weight: slide up for slow, down for fast; calibrate beats per minute for music.
lessons.advanced: Explain with the physical-pendulum idea why moving mass up slows the beat.

lessons.title: Sloshing Water: Basins, Tanks and Bores
lessons.focus: Slosh a basin; natural slosh period vs basin size; why tankers have baffles; seiche on a lake teaser.
lessons.advanced: Explain why baffles raise damping and shift frequency; design a baffle layout for a pickup water tank.

lessons.title: Buildings That Sway
lessons.focus: Flexible vs stiff; Rift Valley earthquake awareness; water tanks on towers act like pendulums; model with sticks and clay.
lessons.advanced: Tall flexible vs short stiff model on the shake table: relate survival to natural frequency mismatch.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Pendulum Olympics
lessons.focus: Stations: predict the period, tune to a target, coupled-pendulum demo, damping race; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Championship: specify a pendulum to keep Nairobi time within 30 s/day; show the design math.

units.title: Momentum & Collisions
units.intro: Rolling debes, crashing marbles and safe bodas: momentum, impulse and why crumple zones save lives.

lessons.title: Mass in Motion: Introducing Momentum
lessons.focus: p = mv; which is harder to stop: fast football or slow rolling debe? Stopping stories build the idea.
lessons.advanced: Compare p for a 0.45 kg ball at 25 m/s vs a 15 kg debe at 1 m/s; stopping distance implications.

lessons.title: Why Momentum Matters on the Road
lessons.focus: Boda braking distance grows with load and speed; overloaded pickups; momentum as 'quantity of motion'.
lessons.advanced: Doubling speed doubles p but quadruples KE: which governs braking distance and which crash violence? Discuss.

lessons.title: Impulse: The Egg-Catching Secret
lessons.focus: Δp = F×t; soft hands extend time and reduce force; landing with bent knees; gym mats and sand pits.
lessons.advanced: 60 g egg at 6 m/s stopped in 0.5 s (cloth) vs 0.02 s (floor): compute both forces and the verdict.

lessons.title: Follow-Through: Impulse in Sport
lessons.focus: Long contact adds impulse: javelin run-up, football kick follow-through, jembe swing; analyze slow-motion descriptions.
lessons.advanced: Estimate: javelin 0.8 kg accelerated over 1.2 s of contact to 25 m/s: average force?

lessons.title: Collisions That Bounce
lessons.focus: Marbles and bottle tops on a smooth board; equal masses 'swap speeds'; line-of-centres idea.
lessons.advanced: Equal-mass head-on collision: prove speed-swap from conservation of p and KE together.

lessons.title: Collisions That Stick
lessons.focus: Clay lumps collide and move on together; momentum conserved, KE not; where the KE went (deformation heat).
lessons.advanced: 2 kg clay at 3 m/s hits stationary 1 kg and sticks: final speed and the KE lost — account for it.

lessons.title: Conservation of Momentum
lessons.focus: Two trolleys spring apart: equal and opposite momenta from rest; measure masses and speeds to check.
lessons.advanced: 3 kg cart moves off at 0.5 m/s as a 2 kg cart recoils at 0.75 m/s: verify conservation numerically.

lessons.title: Safe 'Explosions': Springs and Balloons
lessons.focus: Balloon release propels a bottle boat; spring-apart carts; internal forces only redistribute momentum.
lessons.advanced: Balloon 50 g ejects air backward: explain the boat's forward p with momentum bookkeeping.

lessons.title: Recoil: Stepping Off the Dugout
lessons.focus: Step off a low-friction plank on rollers and it slides back; canoe push-offs; firefighter hose kickback stories.
lessons.advanced: 60 kg student steps off at 2 m/s from a 20 kg plank: plank recoil speed?

lessons.title: Rockets Are Momentum Machines
lessons.focus: Revisit the Unit 4 water rocket: mass out the back, rocket forward; why staged pumps beat single blasts.
