lessons.advanced: Estimate thrust: 0.5 L expelled in 0.15 s at 20 m/s — average force and peak acceleration of a 0.3 kg rocket.

lessons.title: Crumple Zones and Cushions
lessons.focus: Egg on foam vs floor revisited with numbers; crumple zones extend collision time; helmet foam anatomy.
lessons.advanced: Design spec: keep head force under 300 N for a 3 m fall onto a helmet liner — estimate needed crush distance.

lessons.title: Project: Boda Safety Physics Campaign
lessons.focus: Turn impulse, braking and momentum data into posters for the local boda stage; peer-test the messages.
lessons.advanced: Include one quantitative panel: compute a braking distance at 40 vs 60 km/h with realistic deceleration.

lessons.title: Momentum Games: Carrom and Marbles Tourney
lessons.focus: Angles and speed transfer in carrom breaks and marbles; predict rebounds; run a scored mini-tournament.
lessons.advanced: Analyze a glancing collision: momentum as vectors; why does the striker deflect rather than stop?

lessons.title: Build: A Bottle-Top Newton's Cradle
lessons.focus: Five nuts/tops on V-strings in a frame; tune contact for clean transfers; one swings in, one swings out.
lessons.advanced: Explain why two-in produces two-out using both conservation laws, not momentum alone.

lessons.title: Momentum in Water and Air
lessons.focus: Hose jet pushes back; river bends erode the outside bank; fanning air moves paper; fluid momentum in daily life.
lessons.advanced: Hose delivers 0.5 kg/s at 4 m/s: compute the reaction force on the holder's hands.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Collision Lab Day
lessons.focus: Stations: marble swaps, clay sticks, cradle demo, impulse egg test; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Open-ended: design an experiment to verify conservation of momentum with only a ruler, stopwatch and two carts.

units.title: Elasticity, Materials & Structures
units.intro: Hooke's law on rubber strips, the secret strength of corrugated mabati, and bridges built from sticks.

lessons.title: The Materials Around Us
lessons.focus: Survey: wood, steel, wire, sisal, mabati, clay, bamboo, PET bottles; match properties to uses in the school compound.
lessons.advanced: Build a properties matrix (strength, stiffness, weight, cost, rot) for five materials and one chosen use each.

lessons.title: Stretch It: Elastic vs Plastic
lessons.focus: Rubber returns, plasticine stays, wire does both in sequence; define elastic/plastic deformation with bends.
lessons.advanced: Sketch the force-extension curve for wire: label elastic region, yield point, plastic region, break.

lessons.title: Hooke's Law: F = kx
lessons.focus: Hang water-bottle weights on a rubber strip/spring; extension grows proportionally while in the elastic region; find k.
lessons.advanced: From your graph gradient, compute k in N/m; predict the extension for a 2.5 kg load and test it.

lessons.title: Spring Constant Lab: Calibrating Rubber
lessons.focus: Measure k for three rubber strips; rubber stiffens at high stretch (non-Hookean tail); report honest ranges.
lessons.advanced: Quote k as a range with the valid force window; explain the tail using polymer chain alignment.

lessons.title: Beyond the Elastic Limit
lessons.focus: Stretch to permanent set, then to breaking; record breaking forces; safety glasses and low drops.
lessons.advanced: Define breaking stress; compute it for a strip of known cross-section from your measured breaking force.

lessons.title: Build: A Calibrated Spring Scale I
lessons.focus: Refine the Unit 2 force meter: better pointer, card scale, zero adjustment; calibrate 0–10 N with water.
lessons.advanced: Explain how adding a second identical strip in parallel changes k; verify with a measurement.

lessons.title: Build: A Calibrated Spring Scale II — Certification
lessons.focus: Blind-test five mystery masses against a reference scale; error table; issue 'inspection certificates'.
lessons.advanced: Scale reads 4% low at 8 N but true at 2 N: model the fault (nonlinear strip?) and propose a correction table.

lessons.title: Mechanical Properties of Materials (CBE 1.3)
lessons.focus: Ductility (drawn wire), malleability (hammered bottle top), brittleness (chalk snap), hardness (scratch order), stiffness, strength — demonstrated in sequence.
lessons.advanced: Match each property to a product requirement: panga blade, bucket, window, spring, hammer face — justify.

lessons.title: Tensile Test Day: Sisal vs Cotton vs Wire
lessons.focus: Pull strands to breaking with a bucket of sand as load; record breaking masses; strand-count scaling.
lessons.advanced: Double the strands: predict and test the breaking load; explain any shortfall from ideal doubling.

lessons.title: Stress and Strain: Making Tests Comparable
lessons.focus: Normalize by cross-section and original length; why a thick rope isn't 'stronger material', just more of it.
lessons.advanced: Compute stress at break for sisal from Unit data; compare with a tabulated value for steel wire.

lessons.title: Strong Shapes I: Folds and Corrugation
lessons.focus: Flat paper flops, folded paper bridges books; mabati's corrugations give stiffness without weight; card I-beams.
lessons.advanced: Explain second moment of area qualitatively: why material far from the middle does the work.

lessons.title: Strong Shapes II: The Arch
lessons.focus: Arches push outward and downward; build a card arch between books; eggshell dome strength demo (teacher); doorways and culverts.
lessons.advanced: Trace the compression path through a stone arch; why did traditional builders need no cement?

lessons.title: Strong Shapes III: Triangles Don't Collapse
lessons.focus: Push a square frame vs a triangle frame; roof trusses, tank stands, bicycle frames; add diagonals to fix wobbles.
lessons.advanced: Count members needed to triangulate a square and a pentagon frame; state the rule (triangulation).

lessons.title: Beams and Cantilevers
lessons.focus: Ruler overhang records; top stretches, bottom compresses; I-beam and bamboo-split demos; shelf brackets.
lessons.advanced: Doubling beam depth quarters the sag (rule of thumb): explain with the stretched-top/compressed-bottom model.

lessons.title: Tension vs Compression: Reading a Structure
lessons.focus: Rope vs pillar; label every member of a tank stand and a truss as T or C; sponge-beam clues.
lessons.advanced: In a simple truss under central load, which members are in tension? Prove by 'removing' each mentally.

lessons.title: Centre of Gravity and Stability
lessons.focus: Wide base + low CG = stable; topple bottles vs sufurias; line-of-action falling outside the base.
lessons.advanced: Tilt angle to topple: compute for a box 40 cm wide, CG 50 cm high; compare with a wide jerrican.

lessons.title: Balance Acts: Loads on Heads, Bodas and Carts
lessons.focus: Revisit head carrying with CG reasoning; mkokoteni load over the axle; high loads on boda carriers; safe loading rules.
lessons.advanced: Design the loading plan for a mkokoteni carrying 100 kg of mixed goods; justify by CG and axle moments.

lessons.title: Bridge Challenge I: Design Brief
lessons.focus: Span 50 cm between desks, hold 1 kg at midspan, sticks/straws/string/glue only; sketch, triangulate, predict failure point.
lessons.advanced: Predict the failing member and its T/C nature; estimate your bridge's strength-to-weight ratio.

lessons.title: Bridge Challenge II: Build
lessons.focus: Construct to the drawing; log changes and reasons; weigh materials used (efficiency counts).
lessons.advanced: Keep a build log entry for every design deviation with a physics justification.

lessons.title: Bridge Challenge III: Test and Autopsy
lessons.focus: Load to destruction with sand bucket; record max load and failure mode; crown strength-to-weight champion.
lessons.advanced: Compute each bridge's strength-to-weight ratio; analyze the champion's geometry and write the design rule.

lessons.title: Tower Challenge: Tallest Stable Structure
lessons.focus: Paper/straw tower must stand 10 s in a fan breeze; base width vs height; guy ropes allowed or not?
lessons.advanced: Estimate the overturning moment from wind at 5 m/s on your tower face; size the base by moments.

lessons.title: Foundations and Soil: The Ground Is a Material Too
lessons.focus: Compact vs loose soil bearing; why buildings crack unevenly; mud vs stone footings; simple bearing test with a weighted shoe box.
lessons.advanced: Compute safe footing width: house wall 20 000 N per metre on soil bearing 100 kPa.

lessons.title: Materials and Climate: Thatch vs Mabati and Maintenance
lessons.focus: Thatch insulates, mabati lasts; rust, rot, termites; maintenance schedules as applied physics.
lessons.advanced: Lifecycle analysis: thatch every 5 years vs mabati once — compare 30-year cost and comfort with numbers.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Structure Expo
lessons.focus: Bridges and towers on display with failure stories; materials quiz stations; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Write the expo caption for your build: forces carried, failure mode found, one improvement.

units.title: Wind & Water Power Projects
units.intro: The flagship unit: anemometers, a working windmill water pump, stream turbines and the physics of harvesting Kenya's wind and water.

lessons.title: Wind Is Moving Air: Where It Comes From
lessons.focus: Sun heats land unevenly → convection → wind; Kenyan winds: Lake Turkana jet, Ngong hills, coastal monsoons.
lessons.advanced: Explain the sea-breeze cycle at the coast with land/water heating rates; when does it reverse?

lessons.title: Build: A Wind Sock and the Beaufort Scale
lessons.focus: Sew/tape a sock from a plastic bag on a pole; read direction and estimate strength with a picture scale.
lessons.advanced: Keep a week log of direction/strength; compute the prevailing direction and justify with a simple vector tally.

lessons.title: Build: A Cup Anemometer
lessons.focus: Bottle-top cups on crossed sticks around a pencil axle; count turns in 30 s against a reference chart (or phone slow-motion).
lessons.advanced: Calibrate: passenger counts turns at known vehicle speeds (safe, from inside!); produce a turns→km/h card.

lessons.title: Wind Force on Surfaces
lessons.focus: Feel push on card at angles; sail and blade angle intro; force grows with area and with speed squared.
lessons.advanced: Use F≈½ρAv² to estimate force on a 1 m² signboard at 15 m/s; why do billboards fail in storms?

lessons.title: Windmills of East Africa: Kijito and Kamkwamba
lessons.focus: Kijito wind pumps of Kenya and William Kamkwamba's Malawi windmill; mechanical water pumping heritage; what makes a good site.
lessons.advanced: Compare a wind pump vs solar pump for a borehole: energy source pattern vs water demand pattern.

lessons.title: How a Wind Pump Works: Rotor to Piston
lessons.focus: Blades catch wind → crank/cam turns rotation into up-down → pump rod lifts water; trace the energy chain.
lessons.advanced: Crank radius 5 cm, pump bore 3 cm: relate rotor torque to lift force per stroke.

lessons.title: Blade Physics: Angle, Lift and Drag
lessons.focus: Test flat vs curved vs angled blades in fan wind; measure spin speed; the modern curved blade wins.
lessons.advanced: Explain lift on a curved blade with Bernoulli-style reasoning; why does too-steep pitch stall?

lessons.title: Build: The Paper Pinwheel
lessons.focus: First rotor: pin and pencil pinwheel; test blade counts 2/4/6; free spin vs loaded (lifting a thread).
lessons.advanced: Why does a 3-blade rotor often beat 6 for speed but lose on starting torque? Test and discuss.

lessons.title: Windmill Project I: Rotor and Hub
lessons.focus: Build the working rotor: blades from mabati offcuts or stiff plastic on a bicycle hub/nail bearing; balance it.
lessons.advanced: Balance the rotor dynamically: explain wobble sources and fix via counterweights.

lessons.title: Windmill Project II: Tower and Yaw
lessons.focus: Triangulated tower (Unit 13!), tail vane keeps rotor facing wind; safe height for school (2–3 m).
lessons.advanced: Compute the overturning moment at full wind on the rotor disc; specify pegging to resist it.

lessons.title: Windmill Project III: The Drive Train
lessons.focus: Crank or cam converts rotation to reciprocation; connecting rod to the pump; friction points oiled.
lessons.advanced: Measure stroke length vs crank radius; relate strokes/minute to rotor rpm and gear options.

lessons.title: Windmill Project IV: Linking the Pump
lessons.focus: Connect the Unit 8 diaphragm pump; suction line to a water container; check valve orientation verified.
lessons.advanced: Predict litres/minute from rotor rpm × stroke volume at your measured efficiency.

lessons.title: Windmill Project V: Test Day
lessons.focus: Run in wind: measure water lifted per minute at 1 m head; photograph, log, celebrate; safety perimeter for spinning blades.
lessons.advanced: Compute hydraulic power out (ρgQh) vs estimated wind power in (½ρAv³); the honest efficiency.

lessons.title: Windmill Project VI: Iteration
lessons.focus: One improvement each team: blade pitch, tail size, bearing friction, stroke length; A/B test against the log.
lessons.advanced: Design the A/B test so wind variation doesn't fool you (interleave trials); report with error bars.

lessons.title: Windmill Project VII: Data and Graphs
lessons.focus: Compile output vs wind speed; find the cut-in speed; present the performance curve.
lessons.advanced: Fit output ∝ (v − v_cutin) approximately; justify the cubic-energy intuition behind the curve's shape.

lessons.title: Windmill Project VIII: Engineering Report
lessons.focus: Teams present: design, data, failures, fixes, costs; audience of teachers and a jua kali guest if possible.
lessons.advanced: Include a costing: materials, hours, water per day — compare with a jerrican-carried alternative.

lessons.title: Water Power: Head and Flow
lessons.focus: Energy = mgh of falling water; micro-hydro reality in Kenya's highlands; head vs flow trade for power.
lessons.advanced: Stream: 2 L/s falling 5 m: compute available power; what could it run?

lessons.title: Water Wheels: Undershot and Overshot
lessons.focus: History of mills; undershot uses stream speed, overshot uses weight; efficiency intuition; model both.
lessons.advanced: Explain why overshot beats undershot on the same water: which energy form each harvests.

lessons.title: Build: The Spoon Wheel Turbine I
lessons.focus: Spoons/bottle scoops on a bottle wheel; mount on wire axle; rig a string-and-bobbin to lift weights.
lessons.advanced: Predict lift rate from cup fill volume × rpm; identify the two main losses.

lessons.title: Build: The Spoon Wheel Turbine II — Test Under the Tap
lessons.focus: Run under tap/stream; measure rpm vs flow and max weight lifted; graph; compare teams.
lessons.advanced: Compute mechanical power from lift rate; compare with water power in; where's the loss?

lessons.title: From Motion to Electricity: The Dynamo Teaser
lessons.focus: Bicycle dynamo demo: spin → bulb lights; generator is a motor backwards; bridge to CBE 3.2 next year.
lessons.advanced: Estimate: your turbine spins a dynamo at 5 V/0.3 A — efficiency chain from stream to light.

lessons.title: The Ram and the Siphon Return
lessons.focus: Review: both move water with no engine; ram needs fall, siphon needs outlet lower than inlet; pick per site.
lessons.advanced: Site: spring 3 m above field, 100 m away, stream crossing between: siphon, ram or pipe? Defend with head math.

lessons.title: Rainwater Harvesting Physics
lessons.focus: Roof catchment = rainfall × area; gutters and first-flush; tank sizing for the dry term; Kenyan rainfall patterns.
lessons.advanced: Roof 60 m², rain 800 mm/year, dry spell 90 days at 200 L/day: size the tank in m³ with reasoning.

lessons.title: Gravity Water Schemes: From Spring to Village
lessons.focus: Survey head with the Unit 7 water level; pipe sizing to limit friction; break-pressure tanks on long drops.
lessons.advanced: A 3 km pipe drops 120 m: why insert break-pressure tanks? Compute static pressure at the bottom without them.

lessons.title: Storing Energy: Two Tanks and a Pump
lessons.focus: Pumped storage idea: pump up when sunny/windy, flow down when needed; compare with batteries and flywheels.
lessons.advanced: 1000 L raised 5 m stores how many kJ? What bulb wattage for how long at 50% round-trip efficiency?

lessons.title: Community Wind & Water Survey
lessons.focus: Walk the area: note streams, slopes, windy ridges, existing pumps; interview a fundi; map resources.
lessons.advanced: Score three sites with a weighted matrix (head, flow, distance, demand); defend the weights.

lessons.title: Design Brief: Power for Our School
lessons.focus: Teams design one wind or water solution for a real school need (garden watering, handwash station); drawings and budget.
lessons.advanced: Include energy budget: demand L/day, source power curve, storage, and the worst-month shortfall plan.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Energy Projects Showcase
lessons.focus: Windmill, turbines and surveys on show; visitors try the anemometer; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Panel question: 'Is small wind worth it here?' — argue from your measured data, both sides.

units.title: Sound & Mechanical Waves
units.intro: Vibrations through strings, air and wood: bottle xylophones, one-string guitars, debe telephones and the physics of Kenyan music.

lessons.title: What Is Sound? Feel the Vibration
lessons.focus: Touch a drummed ngoma skin, a humming throat, a struck ruler on a desk; sound = vibration traveling.
lessons.advanced: Explain why the ruler's pitch rises as you shorten the overhang: link length to vibration rate.

lessons.title: Sound Needs a Medium
lessons.focus: Sound through a desk, through string, not through vacuum; bell-in-a-bottle pump demo attempt; Moon is silent.
lessons.advanced: Argue from particle collisions why sound dies as air is removed; what remains in a perfect vacuum?

lessons.title: Waves Carry Energy, Not Stuff
lessons.focus: Ripples in a basin move a leaf in place; rope transverse vs spring longitudinal waves; wave anatomy drawn.
lessons.advanced: Label crest, trough, wavelength, amplitude on your rope sketch; distinguish wave speed from particle motion.

lessons.title: Wavelength, Frequency, Amplitude and v = fλ
lessons.focus: Count rope waves per second, measure wavelength with chalk; v = fλ for rope and sound.
lessons.advanced: Sound: f=170 Hz, λ=2 m — compute wave speed; predict λ for a drum's 85 Hz.

lessons.title: Measuring the Speed of Sound with an Echo
lessons.focus: Clap toward a far wall; time the echo over known distance; average ten claps; compare with ~340 m/s.
lessons.advanced: Wall 85 m away, echo in 0.5 s: compute speed and the reaction-time error; improve the method.

lessons.title: Build: The Bottle Xylophone I
lessons.focus: Water level sets pitch; six bottles tuned by ear to a scale; striking vs blowing gives different families.
lessons.advanced: Explain why more water raises the struck pitch but lowers the blown pitch (solid vs air column vibrating).

lessons.title: Build: The Bottle Xylophone II — Tune and Play
lessons.focus: Tune against a reference (phone app or teacher ear); play a known tune; record the water levels.
lessons.advanced: If level-to-pitch were linear in air column, would equal water steps make equal note steps? Investigate.

lessons.title: Build: The One-String Guitar I
lessons.focus: Wire/fishing line on a board with bottle bridge; tension by hanging stone; pluck and measure pitch vs length.
lessons.advanced: Predict the half-length pitch using f∝1/L; verify against a tuner app.

lessons.title: Build: The One-String Guitar II — Ratios and Songs
lessons.focus: Find octave (1/2), fifth (2/3), fourth (3/4) positions; mark frets; play with the bottle xylophone ensemble.
lessons.advanced: Derive fret positions from f∝1/L for a pentatonic scale; mark them with measured distances.

lessons.title: Drums: The Physics of the Ngoma
lessons.focus: Tight skin = high pitch; size matters; warming a drum by the fire tightens skin; membrane modes teaser.
lessons.advanced: Explain with tension and wave speed why tightening raises pitch; estimate direction of change with numbers.

lessons.title: Singing Tubes and Bottles: Air Columns Resonate
lessons.focus: Blow across bottles; straw oboe with cut reed; resonance when tube length fits the wave.
lessons.advanced: For a tube closed at one end, λ≈4L: predict the note of a 25 cm tube and test it.

lessons.title: Build: Pan Pipes from Straws
lessons.focus: Cut straws to calculated lengths, plug one end, bind the raft; play a scale; compare with predictions.
lessons.advanced: Compute lengths for an 8-note scale from f∝1/L with your lowest note at 20 cm; list all eight.

lessons.title: Build: The Debe Telephone
lessons.focus: Two tins joined by taut string; sound rides the string; test taut vs slack, long vs short, string vs wire.
lessons.advanced: Explain energy transmission along the string; why does a loose string kill the call?

lessons.title: Loudness: Amplitude and the Decibel Idea
lessons.focus: Big vibration = loud; logarithmic teaser (10× energy = +10 dB); posho mill and ear safety; quiet and loud spots mapped.
lessons.advanced: Posho mill 100 dB vs conversation 60 dB: how many times more sound energy? Show the log reasoning.

lessons.title: Echoes and Sonar: Sound as a Ruler
lessons.focus: Echo ranging revisited; bats and fishermen's fish-finders; compute distances from echo times.
lessons.advanced: Echo returns in 0.30 s: distance? Then: design an echo depth-sounder for a dugout canoe.

lessons.title: Soaking Up Sound: Thatch, Soft Things and Quiet Rooms
lessons.focus: Clap in a bare hall vs grass-thatched space; soft surfaces absorb, hard reflect; classroom acoustics fixes.
lessons.advanced: Propose three low-cost acoustic fixes for a noisy classroom and the physics behind each.

lessons.title: Noise Pollution in Our Town
lessons.focus: Map loud/quiet zones around school and market; health effects; propose a community noise plan.
lessons.advanced: Estimate distance doubling drop (≈ −6 dB in open air): how far must a 100 dB speaker be to reach 70 dB?

lessons.title: The Physics of Kenyan Instruments
lessons.focus: Survey: ngoma, kayamba shaker, orutu, litungu, flutes; classify by vibrating part (string/membrane/air); invite a local player.
lessons.advanced: Write the physics profile of one instrument: vibrator, resonator, pitch control, amplification.

lessons.title: Project: The Class Orchestra
lessons.focus: Assemble bottle xylophones, one-strings, pan pipes, drums; compose and perform a piece; program notes include the physics.
lessons.advanced: Write program notes explaining the pitch physics of your instrument section.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Sound Fair
lessons.focus: Instrument petting zoo, echo game, telephone race; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Quiz-writer task: one question linking f=1/L to a real instrument, with mark scheme.

units.title: Capstone, Review & Community Science
units.intro: The year's physics consolidated: drills, exam skills, a team capstone build and a community science day.

lessons.title: The Year in Physics: The Big Map
lessons.focus: Whole-year concept map built by the class on the wall: forces → motion → energy → machines → fluids → waves.
lessons.advanced: Add three cross-links nobody else found (e.g., resonance ↔ shock absorbers) and defend them.

lessons.title: Core Drill I: Measurement and Forces
lessons.focus: Speed-round problems: units, conversions, force diagrams, friction cases; peer marking with schemes.
lessons.advanced: Write the two hardest fair questions you can from Units 1–2, with schemes.

lessons.title: Core Drill II: Motion and Gravity
lessons.focus: Graph reading, speed/velocity/acceleration, fall and projectile computations; game-show format.
lessons.advanced: Mixed problem: throw up at 12 m/s from 2 m — time to land and impact speed.

lessons.title: Core Drill III: Energy and Machines
lessons.focus: Work/power/efficiency chains; MA/VR on levers and pulleys; identify machines in photos.
lessons.advanced: A tackle lifts 600 N with 200 N effort over 4 strands: MA, VR, efficiency, and the diagnosis.

lessons.title: Core Drill IV: Pressure, Fluids and Buoyancy
lessons.focus: P=F/A, P=ρgh, siphon reasoning, Archimedes cases; lab-practical style stations.
lessons.advanced: Design-question: lift 100 kg with a hydraulic jack — specify plunger areas and strokes.

lessons.title: Core Drill V: Circles, Oscillations and Momentum
lessons.focus: v=2πr/T, pendulum T=2π√(L/g), p=mv collisions; mini-whiteboard showdown.
lessons.advanced: Cart 2 kg at 3 m/s catches a 1 kg cart at rest (sticky): final speed and KE accounting.

lessons.title: Core Drill VI: Materials, Wind/Water and Sound
lessons.focus: Hooke's law, structures, windmill data, v=fλ; practical data questions from the year's own logs.
lessons.advanced: From the windmill log, estimate annual water delivered; state assumptions and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Exam Skills: Reading CBE-Style Questions
lessons.focus: Command words (state, explain, calculate, justify); structured answers; time budgeting; common traps.
lessons.advanced: Mark two sample answers with the official-style scheme; write the feedback.

lessons.title: Practical Skills Review: Plan a Fair Test in 20 Minutes
lessons.focus: Given a mystery question ('does blade angle matter?'), plan: variables, method, table, safety, expected graph.
lessons.advanced: Add the analysis plan: graph choice, gradient meaning, uncertainty statement.

lessons.title: Capstone I: Choose the Challenge
lessons.focus: Teams pick: windmill upgrade, pump/siphon system, bridge-plus, instrument ensemble, or an approved new idea; write the brief and roles.
lessons.advanced: Include measurable success criteria and a test plan in the brief.

lessons.title: Capstone II: Prototype
lessons.focus: Gather materials, prototype the risky part first; teacher check-ins against the brief.
lessons.advanced: Log the riskiest assumption and the prototype result that retired it.

lessons.title: Capstone III: Build and Test
lessons.focus: Full build; data collection plan executed; first failures documented honestly.
lessons.advanced: Mid-build report: what the data says vs the brief; the pivot you made and why.

lessons.title: Capstone IV: Iterate and Document
lessons.focus: One measured improvement cycle; finish documentation with diagrams and data tables.
lessons.advanced: Final numbers: performance, efficiency, cost, and a realistic maintenance plan.

lessons.title: Capstone V: Poster and Rehearsal
lessons.focus: Poster with problem, physics, data, result; rehearse the 3-minute demo; peer feedback round.
lessons.advanced: Prepare the two hardest audience questions for your project and the answers.

lessons.title: Community Science Day
lessons.focus: Parents, fundis and leaders invited; teams run stations of the year's builds; capstones premiered; guest feedback cards.
lessons.advanced: Collect and summarize guest feedback quantitatively (ratings tally) for the class report.

lessons.title: Reflection and Portfolio
lessons.focus: Each learner compiles best pre/post tests, graphs and build photos; writes 'what I can now do' against CBE outcomes.
lessons.advanced: Self-assess against ten key outcomes with evidence citations from your portfolio.

lessons.title: Celebration and Next Year's Teaser
lessons.focus: Certificates; dynamo and solar teasers for Electricity & Magnetism next year; the class physics pledge.
lessons.advanced: Preview problem: the windmill spins a dynamo — sketch the full energy chain to a lit bulb with efficiencies.
